title: Deadly Waters (Shark Nets)
oneLiner: An investigation into KwaZulu-Natal’s shark nets reveals a publicly funded culling system still killing thousands of marine animals — but now, the public is fighting back.
summary:
Sharks have long inspired fear, especially along South Africa’s KwaZulu-Natal coast. In the wake of a rare fatal shark incident during this year’s sardine run — the first in over 30 years — Carte Blanche investigates a system designed to protect beachgoers: the shark nets and drum lines maintained by the KwaZulu-Natal Sharks Board. But what begins as a safety measure unravels into a story of outdated policy, ecological devastation, and public deception. We join scientists, conservationists, and even a shark attack survivor as they guide us through the reality of these culling devices — responsible for the deaths of more than 33,000 sharks, including threatened and protected species. But the toll doesn’t end there: more than 2,000 dolphins, 2,000 turtles, 8,000 rays, and even migrating whales have been caught as bycatch. The insert follows a journey of rethinking sharks — exposing the myth of the "man-eater," and showcasing how individuals and groups, like the Marine Liberation Society, are going to extraordinary lengths to challenge the current system. As pressure mounts, the question becomes unavoidable: if there are better solutions, why are we still killing sharks in the name of safety — even inside Marine Protected Areas?

What sets Deadly Waters apart is its timing and urgency: this year marked the first fatal shark incident on the KwaZulu-Natal coast in over 30 years, reigniting public fear — and the justification for keeping lethal shark nets and drum lines in place. But the real twist is that this system, publicly funded and decades old, isn’t just ineffective — it’s being actively challenged by the public. The Marine Liberation Society, an anonymous activist group, went so far as to impersonate the Sharks Board to expose the truth and stir national debate. Their bold campaign reflects a tipping point: ordinary citizens, scientists, and survivors are uniting to dismantle a dangerous myth. This insert doesn’t just reveal the ecological cost of outdated policy — it captures a groundswell of resistance, giving voice to those demanding real change.

title: One man, One Mission
oneLiner: After explosive allegations by KZN Police Commissioner Lt Gen Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi that the Police Minister and other top brass are colluding with 'drug cartels', we dig past the spin to reveal the rot
summary:
Since then President Ramaphosa has promised a judicial commission of enquiry and put Minister Senzo Mchunu on a leave of absence. Many have expressed their disappointment at the seeming lack of a sense of urgency around the allegations, especially around the 6 month time line for the enquiry and the fact that the minister is still in his position. But these allegations, if proven to be true, speak to the very heart of the capture of the justice cluster by organised crime syndicates. We will connect the dots for viewers, explore the different allegations and provide some much needed clarity on how all the role-players fit together. We are witnessing one of the biggest shake ups in the history of the SAPS - and the man making the allegations is by far the most senior police official to ever do so.

In an extraordinary press conference, KZN top cop Provincial Police Commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi turned whistelblower – taking aim at the country’s criminal elite. During the briefing, which Mkhwanazi addressed to the citizens of South Africa, he announced that the disbandment of the KZN Political Killings Task Team by high level officials was directly linked to their involvement in an investigation into a drug cartel that has corrupted high level politicians - including the Minister of Police. Since its establishment in July 2018, the Political Killings Task Team investigated 612 dockets, secured over 100 convictions, and helped crack syndicate-linked murders in Gauteng and at the University of Fort Hare. Mkhwanazi said pressure to disband the unit grew after its ballistic experts linked weapons found in Gauteng to several high-profile killings, including cases involving South African musicians.
experts: Jeff Wicks Shaheen Suleiman Andre Vlok

title: SA's Classical Revolution
oneLiner: South Africa’s most surprising, and arguably richest, global export in recent decades might just be classical music. Golda Schultz, Pretty Yende conquering the Met to Siya Makuzeni redefining the tr
summary:
The Core Questions Driving Our Story: Beyond the Soloists: While our singers and instrumentalists are celebrated globally, are orchestras in Berlin, New York, or London programming works composed by South Africans? Who are the composers breaking through (Mzilikazi Khumalo, Bongani Ndodana-Breen, Phelelani Mnomiya, Clare Loveday, W Msibi)? The Choral Catalyst: South Africa's choral tradition is legendary. Now, we're seeing a fascinating evolution: orchestrations of indigenous works (like Thulas) traditionally sung a cappella. How does adding an orchestra transform these pieces? What happens when African polyrhythms and harmonies meet a Western symphonic structure? Education & The New Generation: How are institutions like UCT, Stellenbosch, Wits, and TUT fostering this new wave? Crucially, we've heard students are increasingly submitting LOCAL compositions for their practical exams – a significant shift. We'll visit these schools, meet students and lecturers, and witness this grassroots innovation firsthand. The Sound of SA: What makes South African classical music distinct? We'll take the audience inside a rehearsal where a choir tackles W Msibi's "Zulu Mass" and juxtapose it with a rehearsal of Haydn's "Mass". How do the rhythms, harmonies, vocal textures, and spiritual expression differ? How do composers weave African idioms (call-and-response, complex rhythms, indigenous languages) into the fabric of Western classical forms? Global Echoes: What is the international reception? We'll secure interviews with SA opera stars abroad (e.g., Pretty Yende, Levy Sekgapane, Golda Schultz) about how their roots in SA choral music shaped them and whether they champion SA compositions internationally. We'll also seek perspectives from international conductors or programmers engaging with this music.

We start with what every viewer knows: Classical music is everywhere in our lives, but it feels like a foreign import. We instantly establish the central paradox: South Africa is a world-class exporter of talent (our voices), but are we exporters of our own stories (our compositions)? Editorial Goal: Grab the viewer with familiar imagery and immediately pose a compelling, unexpected question.

title: Bophuthatswana’s Legacy: Nostalgia or Neglect?
oneLiner: As South Africa marks a little over 30 years of democracy, a controversial sentiment is emerging in the ruins of the former Bophuthatswana homeland: Was life better under Lucas Mangope?
summary:
This investigation will: Examine the paradox of Bophuthatswana, a homeland designed to enforce apartheid, yet one where factories, stadiums, and casinos thrived. Forensically assess the economic cost of today’s decay: How many jobs and GDP growth have been lost due to abandoned infrastructure? Ask whether the ANC’s failures are rehabilitating Mangope’s image, despite his record of human rights abuses. Key Visuals & Interviews Cinematic decay: Drone shots of Odi Stadium, Ga-Rankuwa’s rusted factories, and Mahikeng’s hollowed-out Mmabatho Sun. Emotional nostalgia: Former residents humming the old Bophuthatswana anthem, a melody that still stirs pride and pain. Expert insights: Oupa Segalwe (Mangope biographer) on the dictator’s "developmental" legacy. Economist estimating the lost economic potential of abandoned sites. Former civil servants who recall both jobs and repression. Gen Z perspective: Young people reacting to myths of Bophuthatswana’s "golden age."

The North West Province is littered with the carcasses of collapsed industries: Odi Stadium in Mabopane, a symbol of 1980s sporting pride, now stands derelict; the Ga-Rankuwa industrial zone, once a hub of employment, is overgrown with weeds; and Mahikeng’s Mmabatho Sun, a former entertainment Mecca, sits as a ghost of its past. But beneath the decay, a dangerous debate simmers. On social media and dinner tables, some residents, especially those who lived under Mangope’s rule, claim that despite Bophuthatswana’s apartheid-era brutality, there was order, employment, and functioning infrastructure. Others react with outrage, accusing them of whitewashing a regime built on torture, censorship, and collaboration with apartheid.
caseStudies: Diale Kgantsi Bafitlhile Pule Kwena Mangope Herman Mashaba

title: Return to Knysna
oneLiner: Knysna, once the jewel of the Garden Route, is on a knife edge - steps to dissolve its council and place the town under administration have been initiated, but is it too little too late?
summary:
At the heart of this political deadlock is a council deeply divided along party lines. A request by the majority in council for an extension to respond to Bredell’s notice was denied, intensifying tensions. They have been granted a fourteen day extension to respond to Bredell’s notice of intention. Civil society groups and the local business community have warned that years of mismanagement, service delivery failures, and financial instability have left Knysna in a state of collapse. This story represents a national test case for dysfunctional municipalities. With the possibility of imminent elections if the council is dissolved and Knysna is placed under administration, this is a critical moment. Will placing Knysna under administration be a lifeline – or a last resort too long delayed?

The Western Cape Provincial Government has initiated formal steps that could lead to the dissolution of the Knysna municipal council. In cases of severe governmance failure, provincial authorities can step in and place a municipality under administration. Local Government MEC Anton Bredell issued a 66 page notice to the Council on the 26th of June 2025 outlining why the municipality has failed to fulfill its executive obligations, and why intervention is justified. He plans to recommend to the Provincial Executive that the Knysna council be dissolved and an administrator appointed. Elections would need to follow within ninety days - allowing residents to reset the town politically. But, residents are divided over what will be best for the town - some say the new Mayor is turning things around and needs more time, others say, there is no hope with this council in place. Meanwhile, the town is on the verge of complete infrastructure collapse, with sewage spills into the estuary at an all time high, and a visible and terrifying deterioration since we were last there 18 months ago.
caseStudies: Eugene Vermaak Wynona Morris
experts: Anton Bredell Thando Matika Sue Campbell

title: UPDATE: Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi
oneLiner: Explosive allegations from the KwaZulu Natal Police Commissioner send shock waves through government and civil society.
summary:
This week, KwaZulu Natal Provincial Police Commissioner Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi called a press conference about the work of a task team formed in 2018 to focus on political killings. But what looked like a status update quickly developed into a series of bombshell allegations. Mkhwanazi claimed that Police Minister Senzo Mchunu has frozen investigations and attempted to disband the task team because it uncovered links between drug cartels and political leadership. He also accused senior officials of interfering in investigations into political assassinations. The allegations have sent shock waves through civil society and government. The judiciary has demanded evidence, while Mchunu denies any wrongdoing. But who is Mkhwanazi? We sat down with him last year to discuss his controversial reputation.

We interviewed Mkhwanazi in 2024 about his apparently tough on crime stance - we revisit the man behind this week's shock revelations.

title: March and March
oneLiner: In a country still wrestling with inequality and high unemployment, a grassroots movement led by a former radio personality is demanding action on illegal immigration — and dividing public opinion
summary:
Launched in March 2025 by Jacinta Zinhle MaNgobese Zuma, a former broadcaster turned activist, the “March and March” campaign calls for action against illegal immigration in South Africa. The movement insists it is not xenophobic, but patriotic — fighting for local jobs, strained public services, and what it sees as the erosion of citizen rights. The story follows the campaign from its inception in KwaZulu-Natal to its growing national momentum. Through emotional testimonies, tense protests, and intimate moments with organisers and critics alike, March and Marchinvestigates the real grievances behind the placards — and whether these marches signal empowerment, desperation, or dangerous scapegoating.

March and March: Until We Win” takes viewers into the streets, homes, and halls of power in South Africa to unpack what this controversial campaign says about race, justice, and who truly belongs.
caseStudies: Jecinta Zuma Thando Zuma

title: Cupcake sex pest
oneLiner: Explosive revelations from inside a company in Naboomspruit that makes colours for the baking industry. Rolkem supplies glitter, Luminous colours locally and internationally, but many of these product
summary:
But the duping of consumers is only part of this story, because the man who owns Rolkem, Andries Kemp is at the centre of serious allegations of sexual, physical assault and verbal abuse of his staff, insurance fraud, and failure to pay over UIF and SARS payments. Now at least 8 former employees, who have evidence of all their allegations including footage and documents have decided enough is enough and will tell their stories to Carte Blanche.

This is a multi layered story with fantastic case studies who have both visual and documentary evidence

title: THROW-FORWARD: SANDF Open Secrets follow-up
oneLiner: Is the silence around alleged criminal activities in the SANDF finally being broken?
summary: In 2023, we told the story of an unresolved mystery. Investigations pointed to a shadowy faction operating above the law in the South African National Defence Force: the abduction of two men at the Mall of Africa; the investigator assassinated. Allegations of illegal surveillance, torture and even murder. At the time, the SANDF seemed to resist arrest, denying all allegations and accusing us of fabricating the story. But now 12 SANDF members have been arrested on charges of kidnapping, murder and vehicle theft. What secrets will be spilled?

title: DEADLY DELIVERANCE
oneLiner: He went in for healing. He left in a body bag.
summary:
Luke Edwards was 32. A writer. A chess player. A son. And in the grip of a cannabis-induced psychosis in April this year when his family made the call: send him to a Christian rehab centre on the KZN South Coast - a place that promised healing through prayer. Nine days later, Luke’s body was found - barefoot, shirtless, and dumped in the bushes (in full display for the world to see) near a retirement home. He’d been beaten so badly, investigators said it looked like torture. The Tetelestai Recovery Centre said he’d “absconded.” But CCTV tells another story… Hours after his supposed escape, Luke is caught on camera - fully clothed, calm, coherent, and very much alive. Witnesses say he was cable-tied, locked in a holding cell at the facility, and beaten for days by so-called “monitors” - ex-addicts turned enforcers. Not staff. Not trained. Just violent men recruited for muscle, not mercy. And the facility? No doctors. No therapists. No psychiatric oversight. Just scripture, fear, and fists. TRC’s founder, Donovan de Klerk, once hailed as a “_Young Mandela_,” now faces a different spotlight. Since Luke’s death: - Four residents have been charged with murder (as of yesterday). - Three staff members face assault and intimidation charges. - One resident has died by suicide (a week after Luke’s death). - Another was hospitalised and is in ICU after allegedly being beaten for defending a witness. According to Luke’s family, this wasn’t recovery, this was murder. Luke Edwards is one name, but witnesses say he’s not the first.

We investigate a Christian recovery centre where the Bible is weaponised against addicts seeking rehabilitation and repentance.
caseStudies: Henrene Wilken Brad Nathanson Duncan Edwards Stefan Grimsell Michelle Johnson

title: Two South African engineers set free
oneLiner: After having spent two harrowing years in prison in Equatorial Guinea two innocent South African engineers are finally home. We bring you their story.
summary:
It is a story of two men who have spent two years and four months in a prison for a crime they did not commit. The emotional, physical and mental toll it took on both Frik and Peter is beyond words. How do you come to terms with the thought that your faith lies in the hands of a government whose judicial system is corrupt? What led to their eventual release was a presidential pardon which proves that they were innocent from the beginning. During those dark days and nights their loved ones lived only in their memory. With the exception of a handful of brief telephone calls, the only connection they had was with the local doctor and their legal representative of the company they worked for. The men lost weight and the worry lines ran deep on their faces. Both are on chronic medication and the poor diet in prison have added to their weight loss. We covered the story of their arrest, sentencing and imprisonment. Now we bring you the story of how the men coped in prison, how their families continued their unfailing support and calling for their release and the eventual release from prison. We take you into the homes of Peter Huxham who, while in prison, proposed to his partner Kathy, who accepted. Kathy, who never gave up hope, washed and ironed Peter’s clothes every week and packed it away for the day he returns. Frik Potgieter’s wife Sonja was part of the support group who sat in countless meetings with DIRCO and on the street during the protest. Timeline: Frik Potgieter and Peter Huxham were arrested in their hotel room in Malabo in Equatorial Guinea on 9 February 2023 on trumped up drug charges and subsequently imprisoned. The two men were arrested two days after South African courts seized the super yacht belonging to the Equatorial Guinean Vice President, and just shortly after two of his Cape Town luxury homes were impounded. The seizures followed a separate court ruling in South Africa that had nothing to do with Frik and Peter. The two men appeared in court on 22 June 2023 charged with illegal drug trafficking. The court case was a farce as no credible evidence, witnesses, or expert testimonies were presented to the court by the State, nor was any proof presented that the alleged drugs were found on Peter or Frik, or that indeed they were drugs. It was alleged that the drugs were found in their luggage, but this was not ture. Their luggage, combination-locked and unopened, was still in their rooms five days later when their employer collected them in the presence of hotel management and the local police. On 29 June 2023 they were found guilty of illegal drug trafficking. Peter and Frik were sentenced each for 12 years in a high security prison in Mongomo, Equatorial Guinea in a prison reserved for political prisoners. They were ordered to pay USD $5 million each in damages, and additional fines to be shared between them. The sentences were based on outdated penalties for the alleged crimes indicating an unsettling departure from the country’s Criminal Code. In July 2024, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found that their imprisonment was arbitrary, unlawful, and in breach of multiple international human rights obligations. The UN also, at the time, called for their immediate release as their physical and mental health deteriorated, and their families were left in anguish. In October 2024, the South African Parliament passed a unanimous motion demanding urgent action to secure their release. Despite this, Frik and Peter remained in prison in Equatorial Guinea. At the same time the families appealed to the South African government (DIRCO) for urgent intervention and the Presidency to push for Peter and Frik’s release. In a letter to President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, the president of Equatorial Guinea, the families pleaded for clemency. They appealed to him directly as a father and a devout Catholic to have mercy. To support their fight for justice the families turned to social media, calling on the immediate release of Frik and Peter. The petition was signed by 16,000 signatures from around the world. A peaceful protests was staged in Cape Town at the Africa Energy Week which was attended by the South African Minister of International Relations, Minister Ronald Lamola, and his UK counterpart, Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, the Rt Hon David Lammy to find an urgent solution to Frik and Peter’s ongoing detention in Equatorial Guinea. On Human Rights Day, 21 March 2025 the families continued to call on the government for diplomatic efforts to secure the men’s release from unlawful detention and imploring the President of Equatorial Guinea to grant the men clemency. Then finally, on 21 June 2025 the families of Frik and Peter confirmed that the men have been released and are at home. No media was invited to cover their arrival at Lanseria Airport as there was still a certain amount of doubt that perhaps something could go wrong. Frik and Peter were pardoned by the President of Equatorial Guinea: an act recognising that no crime had been committed by the two men and that they are innocent and their rights should be restored. On the same day of the release a tweet from his son, Teodoro Nguema Obiang, was posted: “Once again, His Excellency the President of the Republic has demonstrated to the world his humanism, solidarity, and reconciliation, the values that embody him, by granting pardons to two South African citizens convicted of drug trafficking”. Peter and Frik’s attorneys in Equatorial Guinea are currently lodging appeals on several issues, including the court process, the verdict, unlawful sentence of imprisonment, and the amounts that they have to pay in damages, fines and legal costs. The story In this exclusive TV interview we will hear the stories of Peter and Frik and what they endured during these 2,4 years in maximum prison and how they coped. We will hear the heartfelt stories from their wives and what it was like living without your partner for so long We will briefly summarise the past two Carte Blanche stories we covered on the two engineers, how they were arrested, imprisoned, and the tit-for-tat political game played by the son of the president that caused them to be thrown in jail. ___________________________________________________________________________

It was the moment Peter Huxham and Frik Potgieter have been waiting for ... .to step back on South African soil at Lanseria Airport where their families have been waiting anxiously. It was an emotional welcome for the two engineers who have not seen their loved ones since their illegal detention in a high security prison in Equatorial Guinea in February 2023. Their release follows a pardon from the President of Equatorial Guinea. This brings an end to a harrowing ordeal of anguish, uncertainty, and unwavering efforts by many to secure their freedom.
caseStudies: Frik Potgieter Peter Huxham Sonja Potgieter Kathy McConnachie

title: SPECIAL FORCES IN THE DOCK - Follow up
oneLiner: Tonight we link the shock arrest of 12 SANDF soldiers with allegations of a rogue hit squad in the military
summary:
In late June, two Special Forces members were arrested and ten more handed themselves over to the police as the Hawks swooped in on the core of a Special Forces unit, led by Commander Sunnybooi Wambi. The sensational trial pits the Hawks against the SANDF's specialist soldiers, and threatens to unravel of a web of secrets protecting SANDF criminality from scrutiny. There are two elements to this - firstly the disappearance of two Ethiopians from the Mall of Africa in 2022, allegedly at the hands of the Special Forces and Wambi, and the murder of the Investigating Officer, Frans Mathipa, who was attempting to discover what had happened. The second part is the torture of a former security operative, Pule Nkomo, who refused to play along with a dirty tricks operation at the Thaba Tshwane Military Base in Pretoria and was then allegedly punished by torture by members of the the Special Forces, and Wambi, on instructions from and with the collaboration of senior military leaders.

This is a follow up on a story we did which detailed two murders of which they may be charged. We have access to three people who can testify to the events which lead to the 12 SANDF soldiers being arrested last month, June 2025. We produced a story in 2023 called OS Special which gives us the necessary history and evidence to understand the significance of the current court case in the context of past crimes, and have the documents to back it up.
caseStudies: Abdurahim Hussein Abadiga Pule Nkomo
experts: Hennie van Vuuren Moshoeshoe Moshoeshoe Manfred Schulte Phindi Mjonondwane

title: Paupers Graves
oneLiner: The box of ashes you are holding of your loved one turns out not to be them at all - what happened to their body?
summary:
Pertus Booysen of St Francis Funeral services has buried 11 bodies that we know of in paupers’ graves, after having charged the families for cremations and delivered them a box of ashes. But he failed to issue them cremation certificates, and most people are unaware that they are entitled to one. Or issued fraudulent cremation certificates A second funeral service company Javis funerals in Kuils River is also implicated yet has not been charged and appears to have worked in cahoots with Petrus Booysen. Not only is Javis scamming the families but also the Old Apostolic church who held the funeral policies. Javis claimed additional expenses for a bus to transport relatives and the burial of a body when in fact they delivered ashes to the family. Javis transported 5 bodies to Welmoed graveyard for Booysen yet claims he did not know that the one body was in fact somebody he said he had cremated months earlier. One frail elderly man sits with a box of ashes that he believes is his wife who he was married to for 51 years. His daughter refused to hand over the ashes to the City because she can’t bear to take him through this saga. She only found out when she followed up with the City after reading about it in the newspaper. That’s when 6 new cases were discovered, but how long has Petrus Booysen been at this? And what is the business model? The graveyards fall under the Cities administration, and they accepted the fraudulent documents. But apart from informing the families, removing the ashes and instructing the families to open criminal cases, a year later they refuse to engage. Monica Muller- both her parents died 6 weeks apart. Her fathers ashes have the crematorium tag so she knows they are her fathers ashes, but her mother ashes are what appears to be wood ash and her body was never booked out the mortuary. But the mortuary closed down and nobody will tell her where her mother is? The City cant find any record of her burial. She lives down the road from Petrus Booysen and is prepared to go confront him.

Imagine going through the grief of losing your loved one, the funeral is over, and the undertaker delivers you a box of ashes with your loved one’s name and details on it. 5 months later two officials from the City of Cape Town arrive at your door to say that’s not your mothers ashes, she is buried in a pauper’s grave. They leave with the ashes telling you to open a case of fraud at the local police station. This has happened to 12 families that we know of all by the same undertaker. They have nothing. They can’t memorialise the grave which the City has identified, because it’s a pauper or public grave which can be reuse in 5 years, if needs be. The bodies can’t be exhumed until the state signs the exhumation order. The families can’t exhume the bodies, and the City nor the state are coming up with the funds, or the order. It’s been going on for a year and the families can’t find closure. The City who accepted the fraudulent burial documents, and are the responsible authority are now stone walling the families.
caseStudies: Freda Fortune Anita Momberg Wendy Damon Monica Muller Sharivonne Rudolf

title: Secured
summary:
As South Africa's police force dwindles in numbers and capacity, the private security industry is booming. Farming commuities, privaate compnies anfd even the SAPS are using private security firms to secure them. Its against this backdrop that Magma Security was hire in Hogsback and Dodrecht to protects local assets but their methods are being called into question.

A paramilitary security company accused of using strongarm tactics to restrict access to the forest. A paramilitary security company accused of assault and murder in a small farming town.
caseStudies: Mark Anderson Shane Eades Xolani Nxuzula Ernest Mziya

title: Dodo Nyoka - African Country
summary: While thousands of fans gear up for the Springboks’ clash against Italy at Loftus Versfeld, it’s a voice — not a try — that may steal the spotlight before kick-off. Dodo Nyoka, a young man born in Rwanda, will take to the stage singing in Afrikaans to the heartland of Pretoria rugby. His performance marks more than a musical act; it introduces a bold new genre he’s pioneering — African Country — a blend of cultures, languages, and styles that challenges tradition and defies expectation. Overcoming Adversity Dodo Nyoka’s story begins with hardship. Born in Rwanda (or the DRC, depending on the final clarification), he and his family fled to South Africa to escape persecution. As a child, he struggled with a debilitating stutter that made him the target of bullying. The trauma was so severe that he stopped speaking altogether for six months. It was music that helped him recover his voice — literally and figuratively. Like many who stutter, he found fluency through singing. His journey from silence to the stage is a powerful narrative of resilience. Background Dodo Nyoka attended Hans Moore Skool in Benoni, where his remarkable voice first began to draw attention. During a school performance, his rendition of The Sound of Silence caught the ear of Jan Surname, a mentor who quickly recognised Dodo’s raw talent. What began as musical guidance soon evolved into a deep, father-son bond. Jan became more than a mentor — he became family, helping Dodo navigate both personal struggles and the early steps of his music career. Their relationship laid the foundation for Dodo’s rise, offering the support and stability he needed to find his voice, both on and off the stage. Song Jannaman dedicated to him. Cultural Identity and Controversy As a Black artist singing in Afrikaans, Dodo has faced harsh criticism. Some have accused him of being a “traitor” for embracing a language historically associated with oppression. But his calm, eloquent response — that music transcends race and language — has struck a chord. He often reminds his critics that piano keys are black and white, and it is together that they make harmony. This segment would explore broader questions of race, identity, and cultural belonging in post-apartheid South Africa, with Dodo’s experience as a springboard for a national conversation. Connection Through Music Dodo speaks five languages, including French, Xhosa, English, and Afrikaans. His ability to navigate multiple cultures is central to his identity and artistic vision. He often says that the "Rainbow Nation listens to this music,” and his growing fan base reflects that. His songs blend genres, cultures, and languages — a reflection of the inclusive future many South Africans aspire to. His relationship with his Afrikaans foster family adds further depth to this theme, showing how connection can transcend bloodlines and language barriers. The Springbok Stage Dodo will be performing at the opening of the Springbok vs. Italy Test match at Loftus Versfeld — one of the biggest sporting events of the season. This opportunity places him on a national platform, uniting fans of all backgrounds through music. The lead-up to the match, his rehearsals, and the performance itself will serve as a central narrative arc. It’s not just about a song — it’s about what his presence and voice represent on that stage, at this moment in South African history. Interviews Dodo Nyoka Jan Surname In studio…with an artist collaborating? There may be an artist that you are working with at the moment? Demi Lee Moore or Francois van Coke (Don’t know where the above artists live?) Visuals At Loftus At home with Luna and horses and pig Maybe school? In studio…with an artist collaborating? Demi Lee Moore or Francois van Coke 2 Days Filming 1 day at Loftus 1 day at home with interviews Visuals Access to the music videos. Including Hans Moore Sounds of Silence.

title: SACRED CONFLICT
oneLiner: As South Africa grapples with the tension between Christian theology and African ancestral beliefs, we investigate the Catholic Church’s radical new school policy for children experiencing
summary:
South Africa’s Catholic schools have quietly launched a first-of-its-kind policy (January 2024) to support learners claiming ancestral callings to become sangomas. This guideline, balancing child safety, cultural respect, and Catholic doctrine, ignites a deeper conflict: Is praying to ancestors worship or veneration? Can Christianity and African spirituality ever reconcile?

For centuries, a spiritual war raged on South African soil. Christianity called traditional beliefs ‘pagan.’ Ancestral veneration was branded ‘devil worship.’ Today, that battle echoes in our classrooms… where children hear voices science can’t explain.

title: Living On Cheese
oneLiner: Welcome to Centurion - where a water leak is not just a water leak - it literally dissolves the ground beneath your feet.
summary:
Centurion currently has 63 sinkholes. The ground is dolomitic, and the suburb has many water leaks from ageing infrastructure. Summer rainstorms bring tension and anxiety to residents as the ground disappears beneath their feet. Centurion Hospice, Unitas Hospital, businesses and private homes have been severely affected, not to mention motorists and pedestrians. Currently a bridge has been built in Clifton Rd that carries the Eskom lines, and the Rand Water pipeline and sewerage pipes. These are at risk as the hole gets bigger every month. Lyttleton was originally a farm and should never have been developed into a town. It falls in the Transvaal Basin dolomite rock area. According to a geological map of Centurion, most of the suburb has a mid-level risk of developing a sinkhole, and a substantial portion is at high risk. More than 100 sinkholes had already been registered between 1970 and 2012 in Centurion’s business district alone. The tempo has since picked up. There are no quick fixes for sinkholes. It’s expensive. (R2m each) In the past they closed sinkholes quite quickly, but now there are too many. The City of Tshwane wants Centurion to be declared a Disaster Area, and has appealed to the national government for a R200 million grant to repair the existing sinkholes Apart from endangering lives, the sinkholes are affecting business operations, and the value of properties. Some residents are battling insurance companies to cover the damage. Some have sued the City Council. Drilling of boreholes is banned; you cannot erect a carport/afdak without planning permission. It’s one of the reasons why the Gautrain project was so expensive. They drilled right down into solid rock to ensure the line is stable. It can withstand a 20m sinkhole.

Lourensa takes us on a topless party bus Sinkhole Tour of Centurion, akin to Hollywood's Grave Line Tours (Although being winter, Lourensa herself is not topless.) We visit the Big Five sinkholes in Centurion, as ranked by the City of Tshwane. So far, only one sinkhole on the list is being under repairs.
caseStudies: Wim Grobler Tertius Zitzke Dorothy Wye
experts: Sifiso Ngubelanga Ashika Sudu Jaco du Plessis

title: THROW-FORWARD: On the Run
oneLiner: A glimpse into a world of treacherous waters, rival teams and the promise of a bounty!
summary:
Every winter, the sardine run hits the KwaZulu Natal Coast… And the hunt begins. Rival crews take to the deadly waters hoping for the ultimate catch. We preview an upcoming episode of Carte Blanche: the triumphs, the tragedies, and the crews who risk it all or lose it all. This is On the Run.

Unrivalled access to the sardine run, with underwater footage, drones, intense characters and action.

title: Discovering Makhubela’s World
oneLiner: We follow the inspiring journey of Dr. Tebogo Makhubela — from his humble beginnings in Soweto to his groundbreaking work in palaeosciences, his story is one of passion, perseverance, and purpose.
summary:
The story will be structured around the following six key themes: His Early Life and Roots Growing up in Soweto, being the first in his family to attend university, and the early signs of his scientific curiosity. The Beginning of His Journey A look at his school days, first science projects, and pivotal moments that set him on the path toward human origins research. His University Life Navigating an underrepresented field, rising through academic ranks, and overcoming the barriers of race, class, and access in South Africa’s scientific institutions. The Wayfinder Award and What It Means Understanding the significance of the National Geographic Wayfinder title—why it matters to Dr. Makhubela, to the field, and to South Africa as a whole. His Projects: Rising Star Cave and Homo naledi An inside look at his contributions to one of the most important palaeoanthropological sites in the world, working alongside leading scientists like Prof. Lee Berger. Legacy and Inspiration The impact Dr. Makhubela hopes to leave, his role as a role model for future African scientists, and his vision for science accessibility and transformation.

The piece will explore how he defied societal expectations, turned down a conventional mining career, and instead chose to dig into the deeper history of humankind. It is a celebration of African excellence, representation in science, and the power of opportunity when met with talent.
caseStudies: TEBOGO MAKHUBELA KENNEDY SMITH KENELOWE MASILELA THANDEKA MAKHUBELA

title: Philippolis - A place to catch your breath
summary: In the 1960's the great Karoo through road was built, the N1 highway establishing what was to become a popular road trip between Johannesburg and Cape Town. But the highway bypassed the small town of Philippolis and there was great sadness amongst its residents. No tourist trap, no motels, or immediate job bonanza for the locals. The three petrol stations that the town boasted dwindled to one. Buildings and farms were abandoned as residents left for more lucrative locations. But the N1 omission has turned out to be a blessing in disguise. This little southern Free State dorp tucked away off the N1 at the toe of the Horizon Route has the idyllic atmosphere you would expect of a Karoo town and has retained its old world charm mingled with an air of benevolent neglect. The London Missionary Society founded Philippolis in 1823 as a mission station to serve the local Griquas. This makes it the oldest settlement town in the Free State at over 200 years. Philippolis has retained most of its Karoo architecture. Wide streets, slope-roofed homes, the Dutch Reformed Church (which centres the town) has an imposing organ gifted by the Jewish Community (more of this later) to the Boers after the Anglo Boer War.
caseStudies: Meintjies louw Nicolene Gibbons Wilfred Jacobsen Hanneke Bentz

title: Cathy Scrooby and Small Town Sleuths
summary:
Hibberdene is a small, sunny south coast town. It’s where Vaalies go on holiday but, it seems, also where alleged con, convicted fraudster and alleged abuser Cathy Scrooby chose to settle. Here’s she’s hiding in plain sight with more than 12 open cases against her for everything from fraud through to impersonating and practicing as a nurse. She runs the Safe Haven / Golden Oldies frail care centre aka the House of Horrors, from a quiet street a stone’s throw and a bit from the beach. Nobody took notice of Scrooby until strange things started happening at her first Marine Drive premises. She didn’t pay rent, stories of abuse started surfacing. But as the ripples grew stronger, it wasn’t the police that started investigating, it was a bunch of local residents who turned sleuths led by Karin Loubser and Louise Visagie. Together, they had about 20 volunteers, which included plants inside Scrooby’s den, surveillance and researchers. It’s an ongoing project and the collective are determined to see Scrooby behind bars. What the residents uncovered was shocking. Scrooby is as slippery as an eel and as cunning as they come. Before Hibberdene, around 15 years ago, she swindled millions from truck operators with a fake scam where she sold them trucks that didn’t exist. Scrooby ran a holiday scam where people like Gary Barnard were taken in for thousands of Rand. Even her own attorney in Middleburg was swindled with fake bank guarantees. At Golden Oldies she’s been hard at work helping herself to a living off resident’s assets and social grants. She pretends to be a nurse and between her and the unregistered nurses she hired, Scrooby bought and administered morphine to a resident, that died. Dr Pillay in Shelley beach prescribed the meds, and we have him on recording saying that he was told she was a nurse. There are even pictures of Scrooby in hospital dressed to look like a nurse and medical reports indicating that staff believed she was a sister. Down the road near Port Shepstone, there’s a home for people who wanted to escape Scrooby’s clutches. It was started by a former staffer. There are stories of mental and physical abuse, a statement of abuse by a former resident, now dead. There are piles and piles of files on Loubser’s desk. And over the past 5 years she has been piecing the evidence together to tell a shocking tale of Scrooby’s dodgy past and the present where DSD and her landlord were not able to evict her or stop her. Golden Oldies is operating rent free right now, squatting in Johan Lombaard’s home, still illegally.

Cathy Scrooby is seemingly a career criminal, and the community who exposes her
caseStudies: Cathy Scrooby Karin Loubser Ivan Pillay

title: Blood sweat and expropriation: The Fight for Farmland in Georgia
summary:
For nearly two decades, a community of South African farmers has carved out a life in the fertile valleys of the Republic of Georgia — a land once scarred by Soviet rule, now transformed into an unlikely home for expat agriculturalists. But the same soil that once offered new hope is now the site of rising tension, quiet dispossession, and shifting legal sands. New restrictions on foreign ownership of agricultural land, coupled with state interference in production rights, have left some farmers thriving — and others stripped of everything they’ve built. As Georgia tightens its grip on food sovereignty, Carte Blanche travels to the Caucasus to uncover the untold story of South African farmers who say they were welcomed in, only to be quietly pushed out. This story explores the rise, fall, and uncertain future of a pioneering community, caught between geopolitics, legal grey zones, and the unrelenting demands of survival.

Exclusive follow up by South African media on the South African farming community in Georgia since its beginnings 15 years ago
caseStudies: Schalk Krüger Piet Kemp

title: Prescription for Addiction
oneLiner: In Benoni, the street dealer wears a white coat.
summary:
Legal drugs. Illegal deals. A quiet town hooked in plain sight. Benoni, Gauteng — best known for its suburban calm and scenic lakes — is hiding a dangerous epidemic. Pharmacies and a private clinic are fuelling widespread addiction by handing out high-risk Schedule 4, 5, and even Schedule 7 drugs with no prescriptions, no oversight, and no accountability. This is a story of legal drugs being sold illegally, and it’s happening daily in full view of the community. We went undercover. We filmed it. We found the people whose lives have been destroyed by it. And what we uncovered will leave you stunned. The Investigation: Lakefield Pharmacy (RingPharm Network) • Previously exposed in 2017 by Benoni City Times and reported on as far back as 2008. • Owned by Dr Sello Mashamaite (About Page) • Undercover Purchase: Sold us Stilpane (Schedule 5) — a codeine- and meprobamate-based painkiller known on the street as green beans. • Offered an unlabelled "very strong cough mixture" containing Celestamine, a Schedule 4 steroid-antihistamine — no prescription, no receipt. Westwood Pharmacy • Sold us Stilnox (Zolpidem) (Schedule 4) — a potent sleeping tablet — without a prescription. • Owned by Mr Rufus Theunis Terblanche and Mr Riaaz Gani (LinkedIn) LJM Medical Clinic – “The Pethidine Clinic” • Run by Dr Jean Marc Lomena Mukombola, a Congolese doctor and pastor (Facebook, YouTube) • Locals say the clinic is administering daily pethidine drips — a Schedule 7 opioid normally reserved for severe hospital use. • We were told we’d need to “go in” to receive treatment. • Dr Mukombola allegedly makes house calls, administering pethidine outside clinical settings. Case Studies: Real People, Real Harm "Peter" – Brother-in-Law Hooked on Pethidine • His relative receives daily Pethidine drips at LJM Medical Clinic. • Describes the clinic as “full of people leaving on a high.” • Doctor allegedly falsifies receipts as “sinus treatment.” • The patient was in a car accident post-treatment and remembers nothing. • Peter is willing to speak anonymously with voice disguise. "Joe" – Son Addicted, Brother Dead • Joe’s brother died from addiction, now his teenage son is hooked on prescription sedatives from Lakefield and Westwood. • He begged the pharmacy to stop supplying — they refused. • Claims his son is being charged 3x the normal price because there's no prescription. • Joe will speak on record. "Ashley" – Husband Lost to Stilnox • Her husband became addicted to prescription drugs from a Benoni pharmacy. • She personally bought Stilnox without a prescription — as confirmed by our footage. “They hand it over like it’s cough syrup. No ID, no questions. Just cash.” • She is scared to speak publicly but willing to contribute off-record. Experts Dr Eugene Allers – Psychiatrist (On Record) • Has seen a rise in addiction to codeine, sleeping pills, tranquilizers — all sourced “legally.” • Several of his patients are directly connected to these pharmacies and the clinic. Dr Field – Local GP (Off Record) • Confirms the crisis is real. • Refuses to stock morphine or oxycodone: “We won’t touch morphine or oxy’s. The risks are just too high.” • Warns that pharmacies are charging 200%+ markups to profit from addiction. This is not a fringe drug story — this is a middle-class suburb where doctors and pharmacists are the dealers. Legal drugs are fuelling addiction under the radar, and nobody’s watching. • Addiction Rising: Benzodiazepines, opioids, and codeine-based cough syrups are leading the trend. • System Failure according to SAHPRA: No national prescription tracking. “Pharmacy hopping” goes unchecked. Codeine Care tracking initiative still not fully implemented. Video Evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RaU9NcUq6Z_ecdM8WxS94F6Dr_RMY18I

Undercover footage of us going to two pharmacies and a doctors clinic who sell medications without prescription.
caseStudies: Joe no last name Peter no last name Eugene Allers John Mukombola Sello Mashamaite

title: Haenertsburg
oneLiner: From the highest coffee farm in the land, to rare birds and the tallest tree in the world, Haenertsburg in Magoebaskloof is a village shrouded in mist and a history dating back to the gold rush.
summary:
The town was named after Carl Ferdinand Haenert who came to South Africa from Germany in 1857 and made the first gold discoveries here. Dating back to the gold rush the village has retained its old-world atmosphere with shops built in the style of old corrugated mining houses. Trading posts with names like “Never Despair” and “New Found Out” sell collectables and memorabilia and the bookstore “Memory-Hold-The-Door” you will find a wide selection of books on the Anglo-Boer war and the Makgoba War (a war that lasted from 1888 to 1895 about the resistance of Chief Makgoba and his BaTlou tribe against the annexation of their land). Haenertsburg has the second largest indigenous forest in the country in the larger Magoebaskloof area. For an breathtaking experience of the Letaba River Gorge in Magoebaskloof zipline over the forest canopy will give you a bird's-eye-view of the giant waterfall, wild flowers and a variety of bird species. There are 18 avian species on the Red Data list in the Haenertsburg area. The Black-fronted Bush-shrike, Black Rumped Buttonquail and the Blue Swallow are resident in the Woodbush Forest Reserve where our guide, David Letsoalo will introduce us to the birdlife and take us to the tallest planted tree in Africa. David started off as a potter in Polokwane who became interested in identifying different birds that flew into the studio. He was fascinated by the variety he saw and with the help of the Robertson bible on birds, and bird courses he was able to ditch his day job and became bird guide. David has been birding for 23 years and is a regular bird guide for tourists and has even been interviewed by BBC he says proudly. For home-grown coffee, head for Krabbefontein Coffee farm - the highest coffee plantation in the country. Here coffee farmer Zander Ernst will take us up the hill where the coffee trees grow in the shade of the forest, protected from frost and wind. The smell of raw plucked coffee beans being harvested has a unique smell that is different from the rich aromatic scent of roasted beans. What is a place without its art? We meet Alicia Boshoff, film fabricator and fashion designer from Mystic Creations. “Whatever you can dream of, I can make it,” says Alicia. She has worked on numerous film sets creating props, wardrobe and unique wearable art pieces for award winning movies like Mad Max. She moved from the city to a farm in Haenertsburg a few years ago where she draws her inspiration from nature and wild animals like eagles and owls to create her tribal infused designs using leather, feathers and crystals. There is something mystic about Magoebaskloof that nurtures creatives and gives them freedom of expression. Or maybe it's all that fresh air and mountain water, but whatever it is, this little village is truly magic. __________________________________________________________________________________________________

Haenertsburg is a little village on the slopes of the Wolkberg mountains in Magoebaskloof near Tzaneen in Limpopo. Rising 1,550 meters above sea level, the town is often shrouded in mist and clouds giving it the apt name of “Land of the Silver Mist”. The steepest mountain pass in South Africa, the Magoebaskloof pass (falling approximately 600m in less than 7m traveled), leads from the Highveld of the Haenertsburg area to the Lowveld adjoining the Kruger National Park. The town is famous for its flowering cherries, azaleas and the Cherry Blossom Festival in spring.
caseStudies: Alicia Boshoff Zander Ernst David Letsoalo

title: Journeyman: From Fired to Fired Up
oneLiner: Foreign Special on Trump's policies
summary: As the Trump administration pushes forward with sweeping job cuts under the guise of government efficiency, thousands of American workers find themselves displaced - and increasingly defiant. In this foreign report, real-life consequences are leading to the rise of the "Indivisible Movement". Featuring voices like Anita Wolfe, a dedicated public health worker suddenly suspended, and Kenchy Raglan, a passionate grassroots organiser, the story reveals how citizens are mobilising to hold their leaders accountable. With fiery support from figures like Senator Bernie Sanders, the movement stands as a powerful rebuttal to what critics call a government serving only the elite.

title: Small town: Senekal
oneLiner: A town once known for unrest is now emerging as an unlikely rural film hub — not through major investment, but through volunteers with brooms, spades, and a quiet commitment to renewal.
summary:
Senekal, nestled in the Eastern Free State, made news in 2020 for all the wrong reasons. The murder of 21-year-old Brendin Horner and the courthouse unrest that followed exposed deep social fault lines and simmering distrust. But in the months that followed, something extraordinary happened: people who once stood across from each other found a way to stand together. At the heart of this transformation is the Senekal/Matwabeng Community Forum, born from a pastor’s quiet intervention. Farmers, township leaders, civic-minded youth, and local businesses joined forces to tackle the decay — potholes, parks, rubbish dumps, and fading hope. Now, as streets are repaired and spaces renewed, filmmaker Frans Cronje has moved in, converting the old Sasko grain mill into a full-scale film studio. His vision: to turn Senekal into a rural production hub that builds local skills and jobs, with even PRASA now exploring a passenger rail link to support the initiative.

After a tragedy that thrust it into the national spotlight, a small Free State town once defined by division is now quietly rewriting its story through community-led restoration, unexpected alliances, and a shared vision for the future.
caseStudies: Frans Cronje John Mathuhle Seipati Mbiwe

title: Keeping a promise to Bella
summary: Six months ago, Govan Whittles flew to the Eastern Cape to meet Isabella Esterhuyse — a little girl who had captured the hearts of the nation when she ran onto the field during the final game of the Rugby Championships. At the time, Bella was in the thick of a brutal fight against cancer, enduring up to five rounds of chemotherapy a day. But in that moment on the field, she reminded South Africa what courage looks like. Govan sat on the bedroom floor, speaking to her as if she were his daughter. They connected instantly. Before he left, he made her a promise: When you get better, I’ll come back and we’ll play rugby together. A few weeks ago, Bella completed her aggressive chemotherapy treatment. She was given the all-clear, and she’s back at school. Now, Govan is returning to the Eastern Cape to keep his promise.
caseStudies: Tara Esterhuyse

title: RHINO WHISPERER
summary: When poachers wiped out most of the herd, Justine Terblanche couldn’t just watch from the sidelines. So he moved into the bush, living among the last surviving rhinos to earn their trust and protect them. Jutsin doesn't see himself as a hero, just a man who couldn't walk away.
caseStudies: Justin Terblanche

title: On the Run
oneLiner: A high-stakes, character-driven feature insert on South Africa's sardine run, told through the eyes of the netters who risk everything to chase a vanishing natural phenomenon.
summary:
Every winter, billions of sardines migrate up the east coast of South Africa in one of the greatest wildlife spectacles on Earth. But the real story isn't just underwater—it's on the beach, in the boats, and behind the nets. On the Run is an immersive feature insert that captures the visceral chaos, the fierce rivalries, and the fragile economy built around the sardine run. It's a frontline story of fishermen who launch into pounding surf at first light, risking everything for a shoal that may never arrive. This is about more than fish. It's about survival, tradition, and timing. And it's already happening.

1. Sardine Run Meets Human Drama This isn't just another wildlife story. It’s a high-adrenaline, character-driven human story set against one of the greatest natural spectacles on Earth. The sardines are the hook—but the people chasing them are the real story. 2. Exclusive, Real-Time Access The cameras are already rolling. We are embedded in the action with multiple crews and unprecedented access to the netters, skippers, and scientists. We've captured raw, real-time footage of chaos, danger, and victory—before anyone else. 3. Multi-Year, Multi-Perspective Coverage We bring a deep archive of sardine run footage: Inside bait balls in Port St Johns (freediving with sharks, dolphins, gannets) Netting chaos from 2020 to now (boats flipping, ropes snapping, crates flooding the beach) This year’s footage—sharks in nets, overturned vehicles, collapsing markets. No other team has this combination of past and present visual storytelling. 4. The Story Behind the Spectacle Most sardine run stories focus on the ocean. This story focuses on the people who depend on it—men and women gambling fuel, time, and safety for fish that might not come. It's blue-collar grit meets natural wonder. 5. Unfolding Economic Collapse The sardine run economy is imploding in real time. Prices dropped from R1000 to R300 per crate in days. Netters are giving away fish. The audience gets to witness the collapse of a coastal economy—as it happens. 6. Urgency of a Vanishing Event Scientists warn the sardine run may disappear by 2055 due to warming currents and ecological collapse. This may be one of the last great sardine runs—adding environmental urgency and journalistic relevance. 7. Diverse and Compelling Cast From "The Sardine Whisperer" to the family of a drowned legend… from a father-son boat crew to shark-tagging scientists… and a diver who swims into shark-infested surf—the cast is built for storytelling. 8. Visual Style Shot from the air, land, sea, and underwater, the project combines high-action GoPro, drone, underwater cinematography, and mobile footage. It's visually arresting, gritty, and immersive.

title: SePitori
oneLiner: The unlikely rise of Sepitori—from a township slang born of apartheid oppression to a cultural symbol amplified by an Oscar-winning actor—reveals Pretoria’s enduring spirit and the power of lang
summary:
A tribute to actor Presley Chueneyagae (1984–2025) and his role in mainstreaming Sepitori, Pretoria’s township lingua franca, through film (Tsotsi) and TV (The River). Explores how this "mixed language" (Setswana/N. Sotho/Afrikaans/English) evolved from apartheid-era townships into a cultural identity, now amplified by Amapiano music and Gen-Z creators.

Sepitori emerged in townships like Mamelodi and Atteridgeville — products of forced relocations — as a fluid blend of Setswana, Northern Sotho, Afrikaans, English, and Zulu. It was a survival tool, uniting displaced communities.
caseStudies: Phathu Makwarela

title: Tiny Towns: Napier
oneLiner: Napier is a village with a history as unusual as its present day inhabitants.
summary:
To this day, descendants of the van der Byl family still farm just outside of the town. One of the Van der Byl descendants, married a princess from Lichtenstein. Today, their son remains on the family farm, Fairfield, with his mother. He says if there ever was a dispute with the van Bredas, there isn't one now, and he is great friends with van Breda descendants. Napier has a population of about five thousand people. The village itself is a blend of tradition and bohemian charm. The Dutch Reformed Church, built in the form of a Greek cross, houses a rare pipe organ made entirely from solid yellow copper. Napier’s true charm lies in its people. About half the people who live there were born and raised there, including the local doctor. The rest are musicians, artists, and authors. Among them is Roger Lucey, a musician and former TV war journalist whose music was censored during Apartheid. His story is one of restistance, reinvention and quiet resilience, much like the town he now calls home.

Napier is a village with a history as unusual as its present day inhabitants. At the foot of the Soetmuisberg, it's located between Caledon and Bredasdorp and is about a two hour drive from Cape Town. Napier was founded in 1838 after a bitter dispute between two prominent neighbours, Michael van Breda and Pieter Voltelyn van der Byl, over where to build the community church. Van Breda wanted it built on his farm, while Van der Byl wanted the church on his property. The conflict was never resolved – instead, each man built his own church. The town of Bredasdorp grew around van Breda’s church, while Napier developed around van der Byl’s. The two men didn’t talk for ten years according to Napier residents. This story is told in the village, but is it fact or folklore?

title: THROW-FORWARD: Death at Daybreak
oneLiner: A glimpse into an upcoming story about corruption, looting and animal cruelty at a massive chicken business.
summary: Why has government’s asset manager spent billions running a chicken business into the ground? And are greed, corruption and mismanagement taking their toll? The NSPCA responds to reports of animal cruelty and culls hundreds of thousands of chickens at Daybreak farms, while employees report unpaid wages and board members allegedly walk away with millions. It's a story of plundering in the boardroom – and death in the chicken house.

title: Shadow king: the Bakgatla story
oneLiner: When greed crowned a traitor, the richest tribe in South Africa lost its king—and its future
summary:
In South Africa’s platinum-rich north, the Bakgatla ba Kgafela people were once poised to be one of the wealthiest traditional communities in the country. While billions flowed from mines and luxury resorts built on their land, the community sank into poverty. The money was siphoned off by politically connected elites—led by a tribal appointee who betrayed the crown and enriched himself. Whistleblowers were murdered. The rightful king was forced into exile Now, with help from private prosecutors, the Bakgatla are fighting to reclaim their land, expose corruption, and restore what was stolen from them in plain sight.

This is a story of murder, corruption, and billions spent on private assets—of a tribal king forced into exile, and a community living in abject poverty, powerless as one of their own enriches national and regional elites.
caseStudies: Kgosi Kgolo Kgafela II Kgafela ALLEN Few Louise Du Plessis

title: Scamsters of Blue Hills
oneLiner: We expose a property development scam that targeted desperate South Africans hoping to be homeowners.
summary:
We expose New Choice Quality, a property development company that set up shop in Midrand. The owner, Kamogelo Matuludi, claimed that he owned land that apartments and stand alone houses were going to be built on. It turns out, he does not own the land and the families who've paid him to purchase the homes will never see that dream become a reality.

Blue Hills is buzzing with new developments... but not all developers are legitimate.
caseStudies: Peter Krauser Hein van Hyssteen Noluthando Makhoba

title: Toxic Streaming
oneLiner: He made a living from streaming chaos and violence—now he's behind bars, accused of murder; has influencer culture gone too far?
summary:
There is a dark half to the Afrikaans side of TikTok, one where "drama lives" - live streaming where influencers expose, degrade and generally air their dirty laundry - have reached dangerous heights. In the past few months, streamers have threatened each other, made and received death threats, and even attempted suicide during live streams. But Beetge grew his following after he got into a fist fight with another popular streamer during a live stream. And this is not just a claim other are making, he's said as much during his live streams. The fight got him enough attention and followers to start his own live streaming, during which followers can "gift" streamers cash donations. Beetge's streams mostly involved him bragging about how he would beat up people on weekends, and apparently gained him enough money to make a living from streaming. That all seems to have come to abrupt and tragic end after the fight with Brandon Pretorius outside the Malbroer Pub. Is this a case of social media fantasy turning into real world tragedy?

Ruan Beetge and Gordon Westraad are currently behind bars, pending their ongoing bail application. The men stand accused of th murder after 27-year-old father Brandon Pretorius from Jansen Park. This after they allegedly beat him up outside the Malbroer Pub and Grill in Boksburg. Pretorius succumbed to his injuries on the 6th of May this year, several days after he was hospitalised following the alleged beating. But Ruan Beetge is no stranger to violence. He's a relatively well known streamer amongst the Afrikaans TikTok social media community. And during live streams Beetge regularly hosted, he bragged about how beating people up not only gained him a significant following on the popular app, it also made him money. Meanwhile, the Malbroer Pub and Grill is also owned by Pascal Kaci, the same owner as the Latinos Bistro which we've previously reported on. According to our sources Pascal was not involved in any way, but it cannot be ignored that yet another death has occurred outside a pub he owns.
caseStudies: Lisa Pretorius Juan Melvin

title: Vulture Rescue
oneLiner: In the wake of one of Southern Africa’s worst wildlife poisoning events, a coalition of conservationists, veterinarians, rangers, and pilots unite in a race against time to rescue and rehabilitate e
summary: In May 2025, Kruger National Park faced one of its gravest wildlife crises: a mass poisoning event that claimed 123 vultures, including 20 Cape Vultures—an endangered species. Poachers had laced an elephant carcass with highly toxic agrochemicals to harvest body parts for the illegal wildlife trade, leading to this devastating loss . Amidst this tragedy, a beacon of hope emerged. A rapid response team comprising SANParks rangers, the Endangered Wildlife Trust (EWT), veterinary experts, and aerial support units mobilized swiftly. Their coordinated efforts led to the rescue of 84 vultures, including Cape, White-backed, and Hooded Vultures. Utilizing emergency treatments like atropine, activated charcoal, and fluid therapy, and transporting the birds via specialized vulture ambulances and helicopters, the team achieved a remarkable 96% survival rate among the rescued birds . This incident underscores the escalating threat of poison poaching in Southern Africa, where vultures are deliberately targeted to prevent them from revealing poaching activities. The loss of these scavengers disrupts ecosystems, as vultures play a crucial role in disposing of carcasses and preventing disease spread . The successful rescue operation highlights the power of collaboration among conservationists, veterinarians, and park authorities. Carte Blanche Insert Treatment: Tonight, on Carte Blanche… In the wake of one of Southern Africa’s worst wildlife poisoning events, a coalition of conservationists, veterinarians, rangers, and pilots unite in a race against time to rescue and rehabilitate endangered vultures—highlighting the power of collaboration in combating a growing ecological crisis. Segment Overview Opening Scene: • Aerial shots of Kruger National Park's vast landscapes. • Voiceover introduces the significance of vultures in the ecosystem and the alarming rise in wildlife poisoning incidents. Act 1: The Discovery • Detail the detection of the poisoning event on May 6, 2025, by the Endangered Wildlife Trust’s (EWT) poison detection system, which monitors for unusual behavior. • First responders from SANParks and EWT arrive at the Mahlangeni Section, finding 116 vultures dead and others in distress near a poisoned elephant carcass. • Interviews with rangers and EWT officials recounting the initial response and emotional impact. Act 2: The Rescue Operation • Chronicle the rapid mobilization of individuals from various organizations, including SANParks, EWT, Moholoholo Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre, Briner Veterinary Services, and Wildscapes Veterinary Services. • Highlight the unprecedented use of SANParks helicopters to airlift 39 vultures to the SANParks K9 facility in Phalaborwa, while 45 were transported via EWT’s specialized vulture ambulance. • Behind-the-scenes footage / pictures of the rescue efforts, showcasing the coordination and urgency. ( if any are available) Act 3: Rehabilitation and Recovery • Inside look at the rehabilitation process at Moholoholo Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre, where teams worked tirelessly to stabilize and care for the vultures. • Interviews with a veterinarian discussing treatment protocols and the challenges faced. • Update on the current status of the surviving vultures, those that havee been released and plans for release back into the wild. (which we will film) Act 4: The Broader Crisis • Examination of the increasing trend of wildlife poisoning in Southern Africa, with poachers using agricultural toxins to target high-value species like vultures and lions for the illegal wildlife trade. • Discussion on the ecological impact of such poisonings and the importance of vultures in maintaining healthy ecosystems. • Insights into the collaborative efforts between SANParks, EWT, and other organizations to combat this growing threat. Closing Scene: • Footage of rehabilitated vultures being released back into the wild. • Reflections from team members on the significance of the rescue operation and the ongoing fight against wildlife poisoning. • Call to action for continued support and awareness to protect these vital scavengers and the broader ecosystem. Key Interviewees • SANParks & EWT rangers/officials involved in the initial response. • EWT officials overseeing the "Eye in the Sky" system. • Veterinarian from Moholoholo Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre, Briner Veterinary Services, and Wildscapes Veterinary Services. • Pilots who facilitated the airlifts. • Conservation experts discussing the broader implications of wildlife poisoning. ( These can be someone for EWT) Visual Elements • Drone footage of Kruger National Park and the rescue operation. • Close-up shots of vultures during rehabilitation. • illustrating the "Eye in the Sky" detection system and the spread of poisoning incidents. • Archival footage of previous wildlife poisoning events for context. Narrative Tone • Informative and urgent, emphasizing the severity of the crisis. • Hopeful and inspiring, showcasing the successful collaboration and resilience of the teams involved. • Empathetic, highlighting the emotional toll on those working to save the vultures. Objective To inform viewers about the critical issue of wildlife poisoning in Southern Africa, demonstrate the power of collaborative conservation efforts, and inspire action to protect endangered species and preserve ecological balance.
caseStudies: Jess Briner Ben Muller

title: THE ARTS VS DIPLOMACY
oneLiner: When Politics Divides, the Arts Unite: U.S. Orchestra Bridges the Gap with South Africa
summary:
While U.S.-SA relations face strain, from asylum claims based on debunked "white genocide" myths to trade tensions, the University of Michigan Symphony Orchestra is quietly bridging the divide.

On the very day Donald Trump meets with South Africa’s president, a meeting overshadowed by years of strained relations, misinformation, and diplomatic tension, the University of Michigan Symphony Orchestra will take the stage in Pretoria. This tour features South African soprano Goitsemang Lehobye, a Michigan PhD graduate who embodies the circular exchange of talent between our countries. Lehobye herself embodies this tension. A South African artist thriving in the U.S. at a time when migrants face increasing hostility, she now returns home, not as a victim of her country, but as proof of its talent.
caseStudies: Goitsemang Lehobye Kenneth Kiesler

title: Phakisa Freeway

summary:
Phakisa Raceway in Welkom was once the jewel of South African motorsport — a world-class circuit that hosted MotoGP and promised global attention. But years of neglect, red tape and shifting responsibility saw the track fall silent. Now, a determined group of riders, officials and community members are rallying to bring Phakisa back. Through the eyes of racer and organiser Tobs Motlokoa, we revisit Phakisa’s rise and fall — and meet those pushing for a comeback. The Executive Mayor, local councillors, community voices and racers share their hopes for revival. From rusted gates to renewed dreams, this is the fight to bring back South Africa’s great racing cathedral.

An emotional and visually striking insert about Phakisa Raceway — South Africa’s former MotoGP track — and the passionate locals leading its grassroots revival. From racers to mayors, this is a story of community pride, lost glory, and a second chance to put Welkom back on the map.

title: Dr Stent
oneLiner: What they thought would be a routine medical check up turned into a nightmare . Three patients share their stories.
summary:
The doctor qualified as a cardiologist in 2021 from Sefako Makgato hospital in Garankuwa after he was told that he would not qualify from UCT. Life Westville hospital gave him admission rights and made great efforts to refer patients to him. His practice grew substantially to the point where he was doing Angio grams and inserting stents till the early hours of the morning. His peers in the hospital became suspicious and approached hospital management but were told that they are just professionally jealous as he had double that patients that they have. In the first three months of 2025 he was performing a 130 procedures on average per month while the average normally performed by cardiologists would be around 30-40. Cardiologist then started receiving complaints from Cathlab technicians and radiographers that he was inserting stents into healthy arteries. They investigated by looking at the angiograms left on the Cathlab computer. It was confirmed that many of the patient . had perfectly healthy hearts and arteries. Some of the patients approached these cardiologists for second opinions . They were able to confirm that the patients had no history of heart disease and stents were inserted into healthy veins. Cathlab technicians also reported that the doctor would put patients under very deep sedation, lowering their blood pressure. His modes operandi is to approach patients, often in the early hours of the morning, admitted for unrelated issues , claiming that he saw their blood tests and that they urgently needed angiograms as they were about to have heart attacks and die. It is not sure where he was getting these reports belonging to other doctors. Case studies Ernest is a 49 year old , 6 times comrades athlete without any health issues. He experienced chest pain and was admitted to the ER. ER alerted this cardiologist and he immediately suggested an angiogram. He was admitted to the Cathlab where he was heavily sedated . The doctor inserted 3 stents into his healthy artery. Ernest suffered complications and returned to the doctor who then inserted a fourth stent. (Angiogram images provided) Ernest has developed serious complications . Permanent chest pains and shortness of breath as his heart now has to work harder. He will not be able to run again as he has been left with a serious heart problem. He was admitted to highcare. again 4 days ago and will be moved to the cardiac ward today. He has developed serious heart problems. One of the complaining cardiologists is attending to him. Angiogram images available of his heart before stent and after stent. Dave is a 62 year old man with no history of heart disease. He is an avid spear fisherman and cyclist, doesn’t smoke and has a healthy lifestyle. He went to his GP for a routine checkup. He had slightly raised cholesterol so decided to go for an angiogram at the hospital. The cardiologist claimed that his treadmill was out of power and that he needed an angiogram. The angiogram showed no symptoms but the doctor walked into the ward and claimed that he urgently needed a stent otherwise he had 6 months to live and was about to have a heart attack. He signed a consent and a stent was inserted. He felt extreme discomfort and the nurse in the ward whispered to him that he should have a second opinion He wasn’t feeling well he went for a second opinion and this cardiologist’s tests showed that there were no signs of heart disease but that the stent was causing complications and heart disease. He is unable to live a full life. He can’t cycle and can’t do much spearfishing. He complained to the hospital but they refused to investigate as they claim doctors work independently . They also did not call for a peer revue. His medical aid has refused payment for dread disease as they have found no evidence of heart disease prior to the stent. Jeff Chetty is a 44 year old businessman and avid fisherman and race car driver. He had no history of heart disease but when he experienced some chest pains and was admitted to Westville hospital ER. Dr Duze was on call and suggested blood tests, ECG and and Angiogram. He was heavily sedated and when he wokeup his entire LAD was stented. His angiogram showed that a stent was not needed and not the entire vessel. He was told by the doctor that he needed another 2 stents. He hs instent restenosis > He went for a second opinion and had to have an angioplasty . He was told that he did not need a stent as he did not have heart disease. Jeff went to see Dr Duze and recorded him saying that he needed an urgent bypass . A procedure he did not need. The five cardiologists have complained to their governing body , the SA Heart Association. They were told to walk away from this as they will only be accused of professional jealousy and racism. They have reached out to us asking for this doctor to be exposed as soon as possible as there seem to be no other avenues. They are concerned about the future of these patients. No research has been done to see what happens to healthy hearts when unnecessary drug eluted-stents are implanted. The stents are coated with medication to prevent from narrowing again and reduces the risks of blood clots. The patients are left with life long heart disease. A Cathlab technician has also contacted us. He used to work with this doctor and said that something has to be done.

A Young cardiologist with a booming practice in a Durban hospital had colleagues and hospital staff baffled at the amount of angiograms that he was performing on patients, sometimes into the early hours of the morning. They raised concerns with hospital management and were told that they were professionally jealous . Doing some investigation it was established that some of the procedures performed such as inserting stents were unnecessary and healthy arteries were stented. Patients went for second opinions. it was confirmed that stents were not needed. All three our case studies have developed serious health issues.
