title: 13 Peaks Challenge
oneLiner: One little girl on a big mission: climbing the Western Cape's most challenging peaks in an effort to support rhino orphans.
summary:
Kenzie is the mascot for Fit 4 Rhinos, a non-profit that seeks to tap into the relatively unexploited fitness community to raise moneys to support rhino orphans. Liezl Schoeman, the founder of Fit 4 Rhinos, met Kenzie's dad Gareth through their shared love of running, and soon became acquainted with Kenzie: a determined little girl intent on doing her bit to save the rhino from extinction. Gareth plans each challenge with Kenzie and runs alongside her as they tackle one of the 13 Peaks at a time.

Mackenzie Knott is just 11 years old, but she has just completed her fourth 13 Peaks Challenge. It's a journey of 110km with over 7000 metres of climbing, and it was designed by extreme endurance runner Ryan Sandes to link his favourite peaks of the Cape Peninsula into one "great adventure". Mackenzie has completed the 13 Peaks challenge every year for the past four years, starting when she was just 8 years old. She does it to raise money for rhino orphans, paying for up to 20 litres of milk that a single baby rhino can guzzle in a day.

title: Will the GNU hold?
oneLiner: Carte Blanche asks whether the GNU will last?
summary:
We start the story about national politics with a provincial story - in Gauteng, where a defiant Premier, Panyaza Lesufi, takes the support of the Democratic Alliance to gain the provincial premier position, but then fails to deliver an executive power sharing agreement. It may be that it is in the interests of the DA to stay out Lesufi's cabinet, given the precariousness of government in Gauteng which is a service delivery catastrophe and a state capture nightmare. However this provincial political difficulty underscores the fragility of the national power sharing plan being led by Cyril Ramaphosa. We speak to some of the opposition party newbies in cabinet, and political commentators about the experience of this seismic shift of power and how illusive success will be for parties who are forced to work together to save the country's economy and people, but are still figuring out how to do so.

South Africa will remain in suspense for months to come as the results of the 2024 national elections coalesce into some form of government. But already the failure of Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi to build a representative GNU with the DA shows the faultlines which run underneath the surface of the newly constituted national power-sharing cabinet.

title: Khayelitsha Extortion
oneLiner: Extortion has become an increasingly sinister enterprise in Cape Town, spreading its tentacles from the city to the sprawling townships on its outskirts.
summary:
Extortion rackets have spread their tentacles, demanding protection fees from businesses, spaza shops, salons and even informal street traders. On June 8, a barbershop in Site C, Khayelitsha was attacked when gunmen stormed the salon. Three children, aged 4, 11 and 12 died in the attack. A fourth person, a thirty year old was also murdered. Nine people were seriously injured. It's possible that protection rackets are behind the brutal attack. Two men were arrested and appeared in the Khayelitsha Magistrate's Court, where we were able to film proceedings. Fear stalks Khayelitsha residents, nobody is safe in this sprawling township, where refusing to pay these criminal syndicates comes with a price. Mass shootings linked to extortion have become commonplace.

A Khayelitsha pastor speaks out about the targeting of churches by the foot soldiers of extortion gangs, and how it has become impossible to keep his congregation safe. From braai meat sellers on the street to business owners, nobody is untouchable as gangs infiltrate at every level demanding protection fees.

title: WATER TENDERS
oneLiner: Uncovering the Corruption and Betrayal Behind Eastern Cape's Water Woes.
summary:
The main subject of our investigation is the company Magnacorp, which has been awarded multiple Bulk Water Projects despite a track record of incomplete projects and allegations of corruption. It's notable that the company's trading name has changed multiple times, yet the same owner, Unathi Mantanga, remains at the helm. Under previous company names, Mantanga was arrested for tender fraud amounting to about R300 million, highlighting a pattern of misconduct. We will delve into the details of the incomplete projects, including the Dordrecht Bulk Water Project, Libode Water Scheme Project, River Excavation Project in Libode, and the Ntsonyani Dam Project. Despite significant funds being allocated to these projects, they remain unfinished, leaving communities without vital water infrastructure. The Ntsonyani Dam Project, in particular, has been marred by corruption allegations, protests, and violence. Despite an initial budget of R200 million, only a fraction of the work has been completed, with additional funds exceeding permissible limits for variation orders. As attached, only 20% of the work was done yet Magnacorp pocketed over 60% of the funds. Initially hailed as a groundbreaking initiative to provide water to 40 villages in the deep rural Eastern Cape, the project has become a symbol of government negligence and exploitation. Despite millions of rand being allocated to the project, it remains unfinished, leaving communities vulnerable and without access to vital resources. This project symbolizes the broader issue of mismanagement and corruption within the Eastern Cape's water infrastructure projects. We have obtained email responses from the former MEC of COGTA, Xolile Nqatha, regarding the Ntsonyani Dam Project, revealing attempts to justify cost overruns and delays. However, subsequent actions by the department, including retracting initial responses to the legislature, indicate a lack of transparency and accountability. Our investigation aims to uncover widespread corruption and irregularities surrounding Bulk Water Projects in the Eastern Cape, with a particular focus on the Ntsonyani Dam Project in Port St Johns. We have received exclusive access to tender documents, communication with the company involved, and detailed information on the processes of all incomplete tenders, providing a comprehensive overview of the situation. Magnacorp, the contractor responsible for the Ntsonyani Dam Project, has a troubling history of incomplete projects and dubious dealings.

title: Extortion City
oneLiner: Extortion is a problem throughout South Africa, but Cape Town has become it's epicentre, with violent criminal syndicates operating across the city.
summary:
Extortion rackets and gang violence are not new in Cape Town. Alleged crime bosses Mark Lifman, and Nafiz Modack are currently on trial in two separate cases. They are allegedly the kingpins of criminal syndicates operating in the city. Ralph Stanfield, leader of the "The Firm" is also currently facing a range of charges including extortion and murder. We speak to Randolf Jorberg, the owner of a bar in Long Street, who refused to pay protection fees until his bouncer was murdered in 2015.

A Cape Town business owner speaks out about his experiences with gangs demanding protection fees. After refusing to pay for two years, his bouncer was murdered in 2015. It was a clear message. Randolf Jorberg is now leaving South Africa, after an exclusive interview with Carte Blanche about what has been happening in this shadow economy for decades.
caseStudies: Randolf Jorberg Caryn Dolley

title: Billion Rand Mega Project
oneLiner: An R 11 biliion mega city project mismangaged to smithereens
summary:
Who is Sam Mhlaba? He is the sole director of self-titled business - Sam Comfort Mhlaba or SCM Holdings. But there's nothing comforting about the work Sam has executed on the R 11 billion Montrose Mega City project. The brochure made big money promises and in an interview Sam even said Montrose Mega City would be a step up from the department of human settlements flagship baby - Cosmo City. However, on the ground - the brochure isnt matching up at all because 7 years after its inception over 1000 units were started but none have been completed in 6 fiscal years of works. It's alleged Sam has received R 410 million on the project thus far but the Gauteng Partnership Fund aint budging when it comes to clarifying exatly how much in taxpayer Rands has been dispensed to this incompetent developer.

Carte Blanche investigates what happened to the R 11 billion meant to create a state of the art mega city on the outskirts of former gold mining town Randfontein. It seems a shady so-called developer with close political ties to Paul Mashatile secured the bag and ran with it - leaving a trail of unpaid contractors in the dust along with the "mega city" project.

title: The Joy Group
oneLiner: From the small township of Hammersdale, in Sterkspruit to performing on the international stage, accapella singing group The Joy has become infamous for its ability to transcend genre and continents t
summary:
Each member has a story to tell about how they were struggling and had to overcome personal adversity to get to where they are. Like the group leader who at some point dropped out of school because of no food at home. Another member, Shadrack, had lost all hope after losing both parents and now had to provide for a child headed home. These are real stories and challenges that young people face. This piece aims to celebrate this young group by being in their world. They have granted us access to their school, homes and community.

The five kids were members of a school choir who would arrive early and sing before their practice sessions. They started recording these sessions and were surprised by how many South Africans enjoyed their singing. In just two years, they were collaborating with big names like Madonna, playing Jools Holland and performing at the Commonwealth Games. That was only the beginning; they’ve since caught the attention of artists like Alicia Keys, Sam Smith and Jennifer Hudson who are all queuing up to collaborate with the boys.
caseStudies: Mlungisi Thamsanqa

title: Ozempic
oneLiner: Ozempic: Miracle Drug to fight obesity or dangerous quick fix?
summary:
There's an obesity epidemic sweeping the world, including South Africa, with over 20 million South African adults struggling with being overweight or obese, with women comprising 68% of this group. Now the miracle drug Ozempic offers a potential solution to what is fast becoming the most serious health crisis facing South Africa. Already Type 2 Diabetes is the leading cause of death in South African women. In this story, we will explain how Ozempic works, and its meteoric rise to public consciousness. We will meet people who have experienced tremendous benefits of taking the drug, look at the negative side effects that could arise and highlight a growing market of illicit ozempic being sold illegally online and how easy it is to buy.

We look at the ozempic craze sweeping the world and its impact in South Africa. Touted as a miracle drug to combat obesity and endorsed by international celebrities and social-media influencers has seen demand for Ozempic exceed supply. We get to the bottom of how it works and uncover an illicit market for fake versions on the drug being pedalled on-line.
caseStudies: Michelle Smit Gilly Assad

title: What happened in Heidelberg?
oneLiner: Exactly one year ago, Dylan Bothma mysteriously dies on the R23 outside Heidelberg. Was it suicide? Or was it murder?
summary:
A young man dies, mysteriously on the R23 hiway outside Heidelberg in Gauteng after attending a 16th birthday party. He was killed in an alleged hit and run…but the driver of the Mercedes Benz that hit Dylan Bothma, has been questioned and the case dismissed, an accident. But according to eyewitnesses, the Mercedes that pulled him 25 meters down the road, was the second car to hit 18 year old Bothma who was said to have been walking home from the party at the time. But his house was in the opposite direction of the R23, and eyewitnesses say, what they saw, was not an accident. But the case concluded without the police taking in one piece of evidence for forensic analysis and without one photo in the docket. Dylan’s family was finally forced to believe their sunshine child who was always smiling, committed suicide.

He was a beautiful young man, wrote and played songs on his guitar...as an 18 year old, he had the world at his feet. Why did he suddenly commit suicide? or did he?

title: Takealot
oneLiner: It’s a tale as old as online commerce itself: Where counterfeit products outdo the real thing by making cheaper replicas. But is the online platform, which professes its love for local businesses, s
summary:
You’re ready to treat yourself to something nice online. You hit that "buy now" button, but when your package arrives, it isn’t what you ordered. And on top of that, turns out it's a cheaper, inferior product… a counterfeit or a fake product. That is what is happening at Takealot.com. This has been an issue that consumers have been complaining about over the years on various websites. We have three strong case studies: Naspers owned… CASE STUDY 1: While enjoying a party with her friends, Sally witnesses a child choking and is relieved when someone uses an anti-choking device to save the day. Eager to ensure their own safety, Sally and her friends turn to takealot.com to purchase the same life-saving device. However, their excitement quickly turns sour when they receive a counterfeit product after paying R1800. Disheartened, they reach out to the seller, Blake from Ventira, who imports the product from LifeVac. Despite Blake's efforts to alert Takealot, no action is taken. Fearing the impact of negative reviews on his product, Blake replaces the counterfeit devices for the ladies. He even has the fake products on hand to prove the deception. He has since then had to fight with Takealot to ensure they don’t provide a cheaper counterfeit product instead of theirs. CASE STUDY 2: Paige Mullins and her mother, Colleen, craving some extra protein during Paige's pregnancy, opt for their favourite: PSN Protein by PSN Lifestyle. However, upon receiving their orders, they notice an odd taste and texture, prompting them to contact PSN Lifestyle's Lauren. To their dismay, Lauren confirms their suspicion: they've been duped by counterfeit versions of the product, likely orchestrated by copycats. Examination of the containers reveals subtle differences, with the genuine PSN product boasting superior quality and a distinctive shine. Frustrated, Paige complains to Takealot, only to face retaliation as they remove PSN Lifestyle's page from their platform. Takealot pressures Lauren to have Paige retract her negative review, resorting to bullying tactics over the following months. Despite the strain, Lauren continues supplying her product to Takealot at a loss to protect her brand. Paige's discovery exposes Takealot's deceit; their claim of the product being from the same manufacturer but a different seller proves false, as PSN Protein is exclusively manufactured by Lauren. Turns out Paige discovers a whole host of other products that are having the same problem Lauren’s is: My Beauty Luv, Phoera Cosmetics, baby bottles, breast tape, Dear Deer and Rapid Lash. CASE STUDY 3: Rapid Lash: Wayne le Grange CEO of Blue Sky International: Says they had this problem with Takealot since 2017. Despite their complaints being ignored, they conducted their own investigation in January 2024, ordering Rapid Lash and receiving a counterfeit product (see pictures). Taking action, they filed a charge of counterfeit goods at the Strand Police station against Takealot, with legal support from IP attorneys Adams & Adams. Alleging that Takealot profited from selling counterfeit goods (they take a percentage from all sales), they demanded product removal, which initially met resistance. Only after threats of legal action did Takealot comply.

3 strong case studies; CASE STUDY 1: LifeVac anti-choking device Ashley Enslin is a preschool teacher in Sumerset West, Cape Town who bought the product and it turns out to be fake. She lives in Summerset West and bought the product in March. We can do the interview at her preschool. Nicolette Grace with the LifeVac anti-choking device: They are in Bedfordview, 30 Selwyn rd, Bedfordview. He has the actual fake device as well as the proper one. We can interview him at his warehouse if we want. He can show is the two versions : real and fake of the product. CASE STUDY 2: PSN Protein Paige Mullins is now heavily pregnant now – she says the sooner we interview her the better because she might go into labour next week. She lives in KZN. So we would just send a camera man. But I’ll be online and conduct interview with her, because she needs to explain the video she took of the actual product. We will recreate her ordering the product from Takealot. Then we will have her typing angry emails to Takealot and have her recreate her frustrations and show her taking the product. She lives at: Simbithi eco estate in Ballito, 4 bridelia close Lauren is afraid to speak without her identity being hidden, and I think we can use her to speak as a case study who has been bullied by Takealot. She would prefer we don’t name the product and I think that’s not a problem. She’s taken quite a knock. She would highlight 3 big issues: the issue of how they treat sellers – because Paige complained and wrote a bad review, Takealot removed Lauren for 5 days online. They also forced her to sell her product at a lower price, and she hasn’t made a profit in 6 months. She lives in Sumerset West Cape Town. CASE STUDY 3: Rapid Lash Wayne Le Grange is the CEO of Blue Sky International that sells cosmetics mostly. We can set them up like they are doing a sting… we can have him ordering the fake product, and sending it out for testing to confirm is a fake. We can recreate him getting the product opening it and realizing it’s a fraud. He is in Cape Town: Stikland. ATRAX Logistics is our warehouse. title: THROW-FORWARD: Ukraine
oneLiner: Our team takes a tour of the Ukrainian towns and villages worst affected by the Russian invasion, and asks whether a radical attempt to hold Russia accountable will succeed.
summary:
The 24th of February 2022: the world watched in shock as Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Two years later, attention has shifted to Gaza, but for Ukrainians, the horror hasn’t faded. We visit the towns and villages that bore the brunt of the Russian invasion. Ukraine's government wants the UN to hold a special tribunal to declare the entire invasion a war crime under the definition of aggression. They say that this is what happened in the Nuremberg Trial. Will their attempt to hold Putin and Russia accountable succeed?

A first-hand experience of the impact of the Russian invasion on Ukraine. We speak to those directly affected by and involved in the battles with Russian troops, and hear from public figures seeking to bring international law to bear on Putin and his troops.

title: The Black Mambas
oneLiner: They're called the Black Mambas - and they're the world's first all-female anti-poaching unit - we meet some of the women on the front lines of a desperate fight to save our wildlife.
summary:
Their efforts have paid off, they've been incredibly successful in their areas of operation. What's more, they've proven that women can play a valuable role in anti-poaching efforts, a traditionally male dominated field. But who are the women behind the name? In our story we will get to know one or two of the Mamba's, and find out how their own personal struggles have shaped their destinies and lead them into a life on the frontlines of the fight against the international illicit wildlife trade. We'll meet women like Seargeant Leita Nkabela, who grew up in a nearby village. Her family struggled to just put food on the table, and the Kruger Park was seen as a place for the rich, a place they could not visit. But when her brother became a game ranger, Leita's own perceptions on wildlife conservation started to shift. Tragically, her brother was killed in a skirmish with poachers... So why did she decide to get involved?

The Black Mambas, named after the well known venomous snake, are 36 young African women who patrol 20 000 hectares of game reserve in the Greater Kruger National Park. Kruger is home to the largest population of Rhino in the world and has also been the vitim of the most poaching attacks. Unlike the gung-ho approach of many anti-poaching units, the Mamba's patrol unarmed, and are spearheading a uniquely South African, innovative approach to wildlife conservation. The Mamba's are focussing their efforts on buy-in from local communities in the area's around Kruger - the same communities where poverty and hardship mean people are easily recruited by poaching syndicates. They also provide eye's and ears on the ground in the areas they patrol. They report, track and trace suspected poaching incursions, destroy bush-meat kitchens and poaching camps, as well as remove remove snares.
caseStudies: Leita Nkabela Various Black Mamba Members

title: Hot tea and Apricots
oneLiner: Overnight she lost her voice, her vocal chord's would spasm and she would almost asphyxiate. Kim Ballantines story of loss and hope
summary:
Kim Ballantine’s story of loss and hope. On her 40th Birthday without warning, Kim Ballantine lost her voice. But not just her voice, and lost a means to communicate with her husband and her three young children. She also nearly lost her life several times as the condition spasmodic dysphonia impacted every aspect of the family life. The condition is neurological and most people never regain their ability to speak. For Kim it was also life threatening. When her vocal chords went into spasm, she was unable to breathe and several times she nearly asphyxiated. She had severe coughing spells that could be triggered by a sip of coffee ( everything through a straw). Mealtimes were a nightmare as she would splutter all over everybody. Her weight plummeted to around 43 kilograms. Doctors wanted to cut her vocal chords to save her life but she refused, holding onto her faith that one day she would talk again. But she would have to wait six and a half years. But Kim never gave up hope. Her strong faith was tested to its utmost as she battled through depression and the daily difficulties of her new life. She had to give up a successful career as an industrial psychologist in which she helped companies with their turnarounds. She had to learn how to sign and communicate with strangers who often mistook her as an idiot. Whistling became an integral part of the family life. Her husband Rob Ballantine, an ICU doctor saved her life many times but her inability to communicate put an enormous strain on their marriage. Nevertheless despite the hardships, they soldiered on, and if ever there was a book on how to be married in spite of difficulties this is it. Year after year she prayed and bargained with her God to bring back her speech, but nothing changed. Eventually to save her life she had a tracheostomy – a hole in the throat that enabled her to breath. She told the doctor that one day she would return for him to close up the hole.

Kim Ballantine and her husband Rob's story are a unique story of loss and hope combining faith, family and medical science.
caseStudies: Kim Ballantine Rob Ballantine Natalie ballantine

title: Alaskan Murders
oneLiner: He was an unsuspecting South African, building a new life in Alaska. Then he confessed to two grisly murders, which he documented for the Dark Web.
summary:
Brian Steven Smith, originally from Komani in the Eastern Cape, awaits sentencing for the murders of two native Alaskan women in Anchorage, Alaska in 2018 and 2019 respectively. Now experts believe he may be connected to a series of unsolved murders in SA after he confessed to more killings. Brian documented one of his murders - making 12 videos and taking 39 pictures of himself raping, torturing and murdering one of his victims. He narrated his actions in the videos as if to an audience, saying: "In my movies, people always die," and "People need to know when they're being serial-killed." This story will delve into the man behind the murders, looking at Brian's life growing up and living in the Eastern Cape, as well as his online persona. It will also tell the stories of his victims, and the families they've now left behind.

In February 2024, an Alaskan court found Brian Steven Smith (52) guilty of 14 charges - including two counts of murder, sexual assault, and torture. To the outside world, Brianwas your quintessential ‘nice guy’ - pleasant, quiet, standoffish, and awkward at times but his colleagues put that down to him being a non-Alaskan native. But behind closed doors, he was a man who frequently spoke of his deeply-rooted racist beliefs, was a regular on depraved chat sites on the dark web, and made snuff films. This is a story of the ‘meek’ man turned murderer, who left South Africa to pursue love, and now finds himself facing two life sentences for two brutal murders.

And right now, high-end motorcycles are in demand. These thieving gangs operate in the shadows - a slick, cunning crew that knows the streets inside out. Bikes are easy to steal, easy to take apart and easy to sell. But they’ve caught the eye of team of private security investigators and it’s about to go down.

title: Studio Interview | Government of National Unity - Helen Zille
oneLiner: ... can a Government of National Unity bring change...
summary: Parliament convened on Friday. A Speaker and Deputy Speaker were elected, and a new president voted for. Nothing particularly out of the ordinary in our 30 years of democracy, except it all took place amid last-minute court applications, threats of boycotts and ongoing negotiations on a Government of National Unity. Just minutes before the first sitting of our 7th democratic administration many parties were still in tense negotiations – both internally and with others. A broad agreement appeared to have been agreed between the ANC and Democratic Alliance, but details remained scant. Joining us now for a perspective from inside those talks is the Chairperson of the DA’s Federal Council and a key member of its negotiating team, Helen Zille.

title: Resurrecting Australia's Extinct Tasmanian Tiger
oneLiner: Australia’s thylacine has been extinct for almost 100 years, but a group of the country’s scientists say they will have it roaming the wilds again in a matter of years. Have they found the key to
summary: The Tasmanian tiger (Australian Thylacine) was brutally hunted by humans to extinction in the 1930s, with the last few living in neglectful conditions in captivity. However a team of Australian scientists are using genetic engineering to try and bring the creature back to life. This mission is made possible due to $15 million funding, however this has caused "fierce debate", as many Australians feel this money could be better spent. Ultimately it is a gamble, as the scientists cannot guarantee success. Nevertheless, scientist Andrew Pask is enthusiastic for the future uses of their research, hoping the technology they develop will also help save endangered species from extinction."Regardless of the endpoint, the conservation technologies that we develop, are going to be transformative."

title: Pet travel
summary:
Despite deaths and numerous complaints to the SPCA of animal cruelty ALL Pets Transport continues to operate. Their next trip is scheduled for 19th June. We have a client who film film her rabbit being loaded in Cape Town and then will share the live location so we can track the route. In van Der Byl Park at the Vaal Mall the NSPCA will be waiting with us in the parking lot and as the person collects the rabbit the SPCA will inspect the van. We have case study whose pets have died overnight from heat exhaustion, other that pedigree dog suffered heat stroke and has permanent kidney and liver damage. and was left at a vet in Queenstown. Another animal took 8 days to travel what should have been a two hour journey arriving in an extreme condition

Transporting animals is a specialized and delicate business. All Pets Transport promises to deliver you animal in two days in an airconditioned vehicle, with specially trained staff. Instead animals are crammed into the back of a Sprinter van, from birds to reptiles to large dogs. There is no air conditioning- the drivers are forced to drive with their windows open to cool down the animals and it can take up to 8 days before the animals arrived. Dogs have died enroute- despite being healthy, others have over heated and deposited at Vets en-route with permanent damage, others arrive emaciated and dehydrated. Bad reviews on various social media platforms don't seem to deter All Pets Transport owner Cornelia Van Zyl.

Its the biggest floating library in the world and it comes all the way from Germany. As part of its trip around Africa, it just anchored on Cape Town shores.

title: Missing at Sea
oneLiner: When a deep sea fishing trawler sank off the coast of Cape Town, only 9 men survived, 11 went missing. Now their families are asking what happened and why.
summary:
On Thursday 16 May the MFV Lepanto deep sea fishing trawler were brought back due to some enjin problems. Later that day, the Lepanto carrying 20 crew members went back out to sea to continue their fishing. They were trawling hake 34 nautical miles west off Slangkop light. On Friday 17 May at 15h30 a distress call came from the MFV Armana, a vessel trawling fish near the Lepanto. The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre picked up the Mayday call from the Armanis that the Lepanto was in trouble and sinking rapidly. Within 3 minutes the vessel vanished. The only sign of life were 9 crew hanging onto a life raft desperate to get to the Armanis as they contend with meter swells and rough seas. They were not wearing any life jackets but with the assistance of the men on the Armanis they were brought safely onto the vessel. The NSRI were called in to assist and sent a rescue craft to the site where the Lepanto disappeared. They had to race to the site which was 35 nautical miles away and took an hour. Three more vessels joined the search but there was no sign of life, life jackets or the usual signs like oil spills and debris. The search and rescue continued on Saturday but even with the help of a fixed wing aircraft to scan the ocean, they could not find any signs of life, only a few pieces of debris floating in the area where the Lepanto disappeared. The depth of the ocean was measured at 300 meters, too deep to send divers down to look for the bodies. It is presumed that the Lepanto turned upside down, trapping the men underneath. On Sunday, barely three days later, the search was called off. The decision was made by The Maritime Rescue Operation Centre. Sea Harvest employer, CEO Felix Rhateb stated: “in view of the significant time elapsed since the accident we are calling off the search. Tragically, the men are now presumed drowned.” It is reportedly one of the worst maritime fishing accidents in the history of Sea Harvest, said Rhateb when he met with the families. Also present at a gathering on Tuesday with the families were the mayor of Cape Town, the premier, and the minister of DEFF to give condolences. At a special service held for the families on Thursday at the Cruise Terminal in Cape Town both survivors and family members spoke out. Benjamin van Wyk lost his son Jeremiah. He was asking where the bodies are? Why did they not go down looking for the men? And how can he find peace if there is no corpse to bury. A moment of silence was given for the missing men presumed drowned. One by one the names of the eleven men were called out. In the Isaacs home near Chatsworth on the West Coast, there is so much grief among the sisters and the mother. They lost their 26 year old brother, Johnwill, nicknamed “Jangle”. They too have questions about the accident and what could have happened why they have lost the center of the family so early in his life.

On Friday 17 May the unexplainable and most unexpected happened: The Lepanto, a deep sea fishing trawler, disappeared in a matter of minutes off the coast of Table Bay. Two life rafts were on board. Nine men clung onto the one, the second blew away in the wind. Eleven men could not be saved and disappeared into the ocean.

title: ANC LOSES IT's GRIP
oneLiner: As the election results are announced, and the ANC bleeds, stabbed in the back by one of it's own founders, South Africa wakes up to a transformed political landscape with new hopes but high risks
summary:
In a set of dramatic election results, the ANC has lost its foothold and come crashing down by considerable margins as angry voters turn their back on the party of liberation, due to it's poor record of service delivery and the neglect of it's mandate. In this watershed election, the ANC has lost political control of three provinces: Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Northern Cape and been unable to turn around its fortunes in a fourth, the Western Cape, which has stuck, mainly with the Democratic Alliance. The loss of power comes partly as a result of a surge in popularity of the MK Party which has captured the hearts, minds and votes of the people of KwaZulu-Natal, and to a degree in Gauteng. Despite of and maybe because of the MK party's shift away from the liberal tenants and commitments of the constitution, the breakaway party has garnered support that the ANC did not believe possible. We explore why this shift has happened, and how it will shape the future of governance in South Africa for the next five years, asking to what extent it is a political and ideological move within South African society, to what extent it is show of resentment and to what extent MK's popularity is based on the cult and charisma of the wily former President, Jacob Zuma, who will not even make it to Parliament due to his criminal record.

We have an opportunity to both witness the results of the elections being announced, and explore the reasons for the dramatic shift in power, as well as start to build an analysis as to why voters have turned their backs partly on the ANC, the party which brought liberation and the promise of transformation to the country after years of apartheid and centuries of colonialism,

Returned to Ethiopia and ran 568,4km to complete the run on 22 May 2024 on Day 301 at Metema. Crossed 9 countries: South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Tanzania, Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, Egypt, Return to Ethiopia Country / Dates / Days / Distance South Africa / 27 July - 11 Sept / Day 1-47 / 1857,7 km Botswana / 11 Sept - 25 Sept / Day 47 – 61 / 653,6km Zimbabwe / 25 Sept – 29 Sept / Day 61- 64 / 104,9km Zambia / 29 Sept – 31 Oct / Day 61-97 / 1464,7km Tanzania / 31 Oct – 25 Nov / Day 97 – 121 / 1179,6km Kenya / 25 Nov – 16 Dec / Day 121 – Day 143 ( 1 day no running) / 928,1km Ethiopia / 16 Dec – 14 Feb / Day 143 – Day 203 ( 27 days no running) / 1109,6km [logistical challenges] Sudan / 14 Feb – 27 March / Day 203 – Day 245 (5 days no running – 4 ill) / 1719,8km Egypt / 27 March – 21 April / Day 245 – Day 270 (finish at Cairo Tower) /1206,7km Egypt / 22 April – 25 April / Day 271 – 274 Return to Ethiopia 25 April Day 274, started running 11 May on Day 290 to Day 301 on 22 May (19 days no running) / 568,4km

Keith Boyd is 57 years old and has a congenital heart condition. But he has just become the record holder for the fastest time on foot between Cape Town and Cairo. Averaging more than a marathon per day since July 2023, enduring injury, danger, and bureaucratic delays, Keith completed the 11 000km journey last week...all in an effort to motivate Africa's young people to vote for better leadership and a brighter future on the continent.

title: Disabling Cyclists with Impunity
oneLiner: South Africa has the highest rate of alcohol related road deaths in the world.
summary:
26 year old Dewald van der Westhuizen was cycling with his coach on December the 21st last year, when he was hit by an allegedly drunk driver. He was training for the Ironman, and it was just after 5 in the morning. CCTV footage captured the horrific incident, that left Dewald fighting for his life. After five surgeries, he is recovering well, but has vowed to never return to cycling on the road. The accused, Garth Pasha, was arrested three hours later. He was asleep at the wheel of his car. Blood on his car tied him to the earlier accident, and he was charged with driving under the influence, negligent driving, and attempted murder. His drivers licence was also revoked. But, in a shocking development his bail conditions were relaxed in May at the Simon's Town Magistrate's Court, and he was given his licence back. This, less than six months after the incident.

The World Health Organisation says alcohol is a factor in almost 60% of road fatalities in the country. You'd think our traffic laws would be strictly enforced because of this alarming statistic. You'd be wrong.

title: The Surgeon | Dr Patel
oneLiner: With numerous botched surgeries reported and even some deaths, we ask the question why is the surgeon responsible still allowed to practice.
summary:
The story of Soraya Patel starts in 2017 at the Glynwood Life hospital where she practiced as a general surgeon in Laparoscopic surgery. Within months fellow surgeons started to raise flags about her questionable practices. She would perform a routine Lap Nissen ( Hernia) operation for 11 hours. A procedure that normally takes between 27 - 45 minutes. Her patients would be gravely ill post-op an many spent up to a month in high care. It was suggested that she was put under supervision but she declined. She was barred from ever working at a Life Hospital again. She sued the 4 surgeons that reported her. The case was heard in the high court and the judge ruled in favour of the surgeons with cost. She was then granted admission rights to the Netcare Sunward Park hospital. Surgeons at Sunward raised flags with the Hospital Manager Dr Annemarie Richter about Patel's ethical conduct. Despite that Dr Richter continued to give her admission rights to practice. To this day Netcare Group continues their support of Patel's admission rights. The Association of Surgeons was contacted for advice. The suggested peer review but she refused claiming that she was being bullied by a bunch of men. The HPCSA was approached. Patel started sending threatening letters to one of the concerned surgeons, she followed him home one evening and sat watching him from her vehicle when he entered his home. It left the doctor , traumatised and vulnerable. There were numerous reports from staff members who had been offered money. There were complaints from staff that she altered prescriptions - photos were taken by staff. Drains were incorrectly connected but Patel blamed staff. She also removed ICU files. Hospital security had to retrieve the files but some of them had already been altered. Patel also allowed her colleague Prof Ghoor to perform surgeries on patients without the patient knowledge or consent. The doctors also reported her disrespect for the Hypocratic Oath. We have obtained a list of patients deceased after Patel performed surgery. Eventually she was barred from practicing at any Netcare Facility in SA. Patel took legal action agains the doctors that reported her. They are unable and not willing to speak to CB as the case is still pending. Patel then gained admission rights from a private clinic in Kempton Park called Arwyp. She was given admission by the very same person that had her barred from Netcare - Zakeriah Esterhuizen. He moved from Sunward to Arwyp. It is at Arwyp that she performed many questionable surgeries on our case studies.

We were approached by numerous ex-patients of Dr Soraya Patel about botched operations performed on them by the doctor and the devastating effect it has had on their physical and mental health. The investigation also uncovered that in 5 years , the HPCSA has done nothing to stop the doctor after damning evidence was reported.
caseStudies: Rudi Claase Hennie van Staden Assim Alli Christo Jacobs Reece Trumpelman Elzette Gouws

title: Tristram Horton Neuro
summary: With 98 Neurosurgeons in South Africa, these doctors are part of an elite inner circle. They are also big money spinners for private hospitals, as neurosurgery is specialised, expensive and means ICU time. Tristram Horton came to South Africa from the USA in 2019, marketing himself as a Neurosurgeon with a double fellowship, which is rare on the continent. After two years in state, he was quickly picked up by multiple private hospitals. A few months ago we got a tip off that Horton was not the golden boy he was being selling himself as, and was a danger to the patients he was performing brain surgery on. What followed was a hard investigation into an elite boys club, where no-one was willing to speak out no matter the cost to patient. The world of private medicine revealed itself to be a medical mafia, where money trumps everything. And Tristram Horton is money spinner.

title: Limpopo Bridge Bus Crash
oneLiner: We take a closer look at the Limpopo bridge where 44 pilgrims were killed on the Easter weekend. Was it a speeding bus driver, or did lack of maintenance contribute to the accident?
summary:
The tragic accident killed 44 pilgrims from Botswana on Maundy Thursday, as they travelled to the Easter celebrations at St Engenas ZCC in Moria. Only one 8-year-old girl miraculously survived. The Limpopo Transport MEC was quick to point out 'the human factor' as the reason for the crash. Back in Botswana the victims were given a State funeral and a mass burial - except for the 26-year-old bus driver who was ostracised in death and buried separately in his home village. On closer inspection we expose the dire lack of maintenance on this extremely hazardous bit of road - a steep 3 km downhill and a sharp left-turn over the highest bridge in Limpopo. Google Streetview images show no maintenance of broken barriers in 2022 and 2023 SANRAL is responsible for this road, but a tender that was issued last year for Consulting Engineer Services for Routine Road Maintenance of the R518 was cancelled. In 2018 photographs of a truck accident on the bridge show damage to the concrete barriers that was never repaired. Video footage by passing motorists over the years also proves the point, as does drone footage shot by Elisha P Tungamirai 8 months ago. He writes: "Having personally visited the Mmamatlakala Bridge on the R518 on October 14th, 2023, I used my drone to capture the state of the barriers, particularly noting the dangerous terrain and the potential danger posed by a fall." Elisha just happens to be Structural Engineer specialising in bridges. SANRAL is responsible for this road, but a tender that was issued last year for Consulting Engineer Services for Routine Road Maintenance of the R518 was cancelled in December.

An interview with Road Safety Engineer Dr Louis Roodt, one of the experts who wrote the South African Road Restraint Systems Manual for the RTMC in 2022. He believes the damage to the temporary concrete barriers over the years has never been repaired. Although the height of 800mm meets the minimum safety requirements, they are not intact in places. The lack of maintenance by SANRAL is to blame for snagging the bus and flipping it over as it vaulted the bridge. Instead of possibly mitigating any damage, it made the accident much worse. Also, the fact that the outer steel barrier has been missing for a number of years offered no safety restraint and contributed to the loss of life.
caseStudies: Gaolebale Siako Lauryn Siako
experts: Louis Roodt Elisha P Tungamirai Reginald Demana Sindisiwe Chikunga

title: Foreign Special | Faking It
oneLiner: This story goes inside the counterfeit fashion industry...
summary:
International crime syndicates have made Manchester the counterfeit capital of the UK – the city is the engine of fake fashion, pumping it out across Europe. Young people are nowadays very open about wearing fake designer goods: "you even have the tags on, as if you bought it from the brand" says one woman. The Manchester police force tasked with combating the trade prepares to raid a counterfeiting hub. They expect to uncover an expansive criminal network: "they're not just going to be concerned with counterfeiting, they're going to be associated with lots of other avenues of criminality that they're going to exploit" says Detective Neil Blackwood. A lot of the people buying the goods don't realise that their money is being used to fund other criminal activities, even terrorism. "Hezbollah has used it heavily...first they sell counterfeits, and then they buy weapons from it" says Elke Biechele, CEO of financial threat detection platform RisikoTek.

With fake designer brands flooding the market, it is extremely hard for authorities to uncover who is behind the counterfeit fashion business. The gangs operating this lucrative trade are not only responsible for fake brands, but also human trafficking, money laundering and even terrorism.

title: 30 Jaar van Demokrasie
oneLiner: kykNET vier Vryheidsdag met die uitsending van ’n spesiale 90 minuut lange Carte Blanche-program, wat terugkyk op drie dekades van demokrasie in Suid-Afrika.
summary:
Dertig jaar ná die land se eerste vrye, regverdige, demokratiese verkiesing in 1994, reis die Carte Blanche-span deur Suid-Afrika om ’n groot en kleurvolle verskeidenheid mense te ontmoet wat hul werklikhede, drome en hoop vir die toekoms deel. 30 Jaar van Demokrasie is nie ’n geskiedenis van post-apartheid-Suid-Afrika of ’n politieke ontleding en voorspelling van die land se toekoms nie. Dis ’n speurtog op soek na ’n dieper verstaan van hoe Suid-Afrikaners die afgelope dertig jaar in hierdie land ervaar het en hoe dit hul identiteit gevorm het. Die program vra ons mense of hulle nog glo dat hul hoop, wense en behoeftes in die toekoms verwesenlik sal word. “Die Carte Blanche-span het die snelweë, strate en agterpaaie gevat om met Suid-Afrikaners uit heel verskillende leefwêrelde in hul huise te praat: van ’n Sandton-sjef tot ’n landelike hoofman, ’n Durbanse straatkunstenaar tot ’n mediese student, en ’n advokaat tot ’n taxibaas,” sê Waldimar Pelser, die direkteur van Premium-kanale by MultiChoice. “Ons dink ons ken Suid-Afrika omdat ons die alledaagse werklikhede beleef – maar hoe dikwels oorweeg ons die geleefde ervarings van ’n wyer spektrum van die land se inwoners om te probeer verstaan wat mense se hoop vir hul land is?” Die geskiedenis van Suid-Afrika is een van migrasie, verplasing, behoort, ballingskap en weggaan van die huis om elders nuwe geleenthede te soek. Dit is ook ’n geskiedenis vol voorbeelde van veerkragtigheid en solidariteit. 30 Jaar van Demokrasie fokus op die landskap en die verskillende uitdagings wat mense in hul daaglikse lewens in vyf van ons belangrikste provinsies ervaar. Daar is stories oor humor, verlies, gemeenskap, hoop en vrees in ’n land wat dikwels verdeeld is, maar soms onverwags en vreugdevol verenig word. Die program skep met kommentaar die historiese konteks vir die stories van Suid-Afrikaners oor waar hulle nou staan ná drie dekades van vryheid en demokrasie. 30 Jaar van Demokrasie word op Saterdag 27 April om 20:00 uitgesaai. Jy kan dit ook stroom op DStv Stream en ná die uitsending op DStv Catch Up daarna kyk. Neem deel aan die gesprek op X, Instagram, TikTok en Facebook deur die hutsmerk #CarteBlanche te gebruik.

kykNET vier Vryheidsdag met die uitsending van ’n spesiale 90 minuut lange Carte Blanche-program, wat terugkyk op drie dekades van demokrasie in Suid-Afrika, op Saterdag 27 April om 20:00. Carte Blanche: Is ons demokrasie ná 30 jaar kapoet? vertel die verhaal van Suid-Afrika en haar mense vanaf die oomblik toe demokrasie begin het, verken die pad wat ons tot hier gebring het en vra hoe die ideale bestemming lyk.

title: UPDATE: A hard knock life
oneLiner: A chapter finally closes on the saga of the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre in Alldays, which has been handed over to the Dirisanang Drop-in Centre after a decade of infighting, politics and alleged frau
summary:
Last year, we visited the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre in Alldays, Limpopo. It was built on Municipality land in 2014, with funds raised by Swedish businessman Leith Rahmqvist. Although the new building was promised to Dirisanang Drop-In Centre, which supports vulnerable local children, it was never handed over. For a decade, over 100 children did not set foot in the centre, and were instead left to eat and do their aftercare activities in a corrugated iron shack. But after we took our questions to the Blouberg Local Municipality, Rahmqvist left South Africa, resigning from the Mapungubwe Foundation Board. Last month, the happy ending this community has waited so long for finally arrived, as the building was officially handed over to the Diriseneng Drop-in Centre.

We rarely get the chance to see a story have a lasting positive impact. But our investigation into the conflict plaguing the community of Alldays, Limpopo, has produced a happy ending.

title: MADSWIMMERS Swimming for Climate Change
summary: Currently, the world’s highest Lake is at 5,930 metres above sea level (masl) and the highest body of water is at 6,400 masl. The Himalayas currently host the second highest lake in the world. Ojos del Salado the volcanic crater lake in Argentina is the highest. But as the planet warms up more lakes are being created at even higher altitudes. Reports from sherpas on Mount Everest say there is a new lake in the Himalayas a higher one created by climate change. If they are right this is the highest body of water in the world. Its meant to be somewhere on Putha Hiunchuli (Himalayas) which stands at 7,246 metres above sea level. Six ‘mad’ swimmers, from different countries and backgrounds, are going to attempt to reach this body of water and then swim it. These are ‘ordinary people’, some with no mountaineering or extreme swimming experience. Call them irresponsible danger freaks but this an expedition led by Jean Craven, of Madswimmers, South Africa. What they do is extreme physical feats to raise money for charities.
caseStudies: Neo Mokuene Deniz Kayadelen Jean Craven

title: The MK whistleblower
summary:
As South Africa approaches an unpredictable and possibly volatile election, explosive allegations expose one of the newest parties on the block. The MK party led by former president Jacob Zuma. This fledgeling party is already mired in controversy not least because its controversial leader Jacob Zuma has threatened to abolish the constitution if he gets elected. Also hanging in the balance is whether or not he can legally lead this party to the polls due to an earlier prison sentence. Now one of his earliest supporters has come forward to reveal how the MK party has allegedly committed electoral fraud by stealing identities in order to meet the requirements to make it onto the ballot.

We have on-camera interview with self-styled whistleblower Lennox Ntsodo who confesses how he helped to forge signatures to get the MK party on to the ballot paper. But we also test the information he gives us to establish whether he is telling the truth, including testing the evidence he has given us against the names and numbers of 120 people in Steenberg, Cape Town, who were on the list he alleges was submitted to Parliament. This is a development on the story that was broken a fortnight ago when his allegations were first aired.
caseStudies: Chantel Adam Tasneemah Paulse Astrid Isaacs
experts: Sy Mamabola Lennox Ntsodo Nhlamulo Ndhlela

title: Steam Locomotives
oneLiner: It's the largest collection of working narrow gauge steam locomotives in the world and it's nestled at the foot of the majestic Maluti mountains in South Africa.
summary:
Sandstone Estates in the Eastern Free State attracts international tourists for its collection of steam locomotives. Visitors are able to step into a bygone era and witness these locomotives in action. They are lovingly maintained and many remain in working condition. A 26km long railway line was built on the 8,000 hectare farm, and a "steam festival" is held annually for train enthusiasts. The festival was put on hold this year, as roads in the area are being repaired, but its hoped they will return next year.

Sandstone Estates, in the Eastern Free State, has the largest collection of narrow gauge locomotives and rolling stock in the world.
caseStudies: Gert Jubileus Bryne Keta

title: THROW-FORWARD: Child soldiers
oneLiner: The story of a lost generation of unloved, angry youths, growing up with a predisposition towards danger, drugs, and violence.
summary:
The Cape Flats: a place where poverty, drug addiction and social disintegration mean that children grow up without much of a future. Where many, disillusioned and seeking a sense of belonging, find themselves joining gangs, involved in violence and addicted to drugs even before they reach their teens. And where those who resist the gangs' invitation may find themselves paying with their lives. Carte Blanche speaks to these "child soldiers" and asks how their innocence might be protected.

This is a story of young boys who spend their pastimes carrying rifles and peddling drugs, instead of playing pretend as superheroes or racing toy cars with friends; where children as young as nine are recruited into gangs and turned into killers.

title: THROWFORWARD | 30 YD DOCCIE

title: EXPLAINER | Hunting with the hawks
oneLiner: ... Hunting with Hawks reveals untold stories from this elite police unit
summary: The Hawks, South Africa’s elite crime-fighting force, have put scores of our worst criminals behind bars. In this book, investigative journalist Graham Coetzer offers us a rare glimpse into the secretive world of this top police unit. While exposing the deviousness of South Africa’s dangerous criminals, Hunting with the Hawks is also an ode to the hard work and dedication of the best of our police service.

title: NSFAS fiasco
oneLiner: As we stand amidst the chaos gripping NSFAS, marked by the removal of Ernest Khosa and the dissolution of its board, coupled with students taking to the streets in protest (tragically leading to a stu
summary:
The narrative kicks off against the backdrop of the ongoing NSFAS saga: depending on how editorial wants to proceed: we could engage in a student interviews, encapsulate the unfolding news. It's essential to trace back its origins, recounting how NSFAS emerged as a hard-won victory during the 'fees must fall' movement. We'll revisit our past reports, where students passionately articulated their needs and aspirations. This journey illuminates how NSFAS evolved from a symbol of student resistance to a pivotal institution in higher education funding. TREATMENT: I have spoken to Mias and he has a lot of ideas of how we can achieve a dark, shadowy feel for the story. He is going to go through plug ins this weekend and also look at options for Peter to then copy on shoot. We have decided that we will have two different grades for the two brothers, and the feel will all depend on the lighting. He suggests Peter uses different colours for the lights to give each "brother" their own tint. We will tastefully dramatize the brothers - and "hint" at the corrupt activities. I have sent them both Floris' story to show them what he did with the photos, and Mias says we can definitely do something like that.

By using the narrative of the Ntumba brothers we will explain how corruption and mismanagement by board led to NSFAS's downfall, shedding light on their questionable dealings and revealing the systemic issues plaguing the organization.
caseStudies: Rudi Heyneke Petrus Mokoena Cwayita Kalenga NSFAS NSFAS

title: Elections | The Underdogs
oneLiner: Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot?
summary:
Premise: Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot? There are 325 political parties who will be taking part in this year’s elections. But standing outside the confines of a long-held electoral party system are the outliers: 11 independent candidates who are going against the grain -who believe they can make a difference with only one seat. https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/political-parties-independent-candidates-sign-code-conduct Why? Voters are desperate for alternatives and some people online have been pushing the independent candidate option as a viable one - but is it? In order to answer this question, we spoke to several independent candidates to establish how they will go about instituting impactful changes. Repeatedly, all except one - Anele Mda - stated they are limited as they only have one seat. Begging the question, why pursue independent candidacy if one already feels limited and powerless. In addition, as they are all championing varying issues it provides an opportunity to debate some of the key voter concerns.

Independent candidates are a new addition to South Africa's democracy. What does an independent candidates election campaign look like - is it enough and IF they secure the seat they dream of - will IT be enough to make the level of impact this country needs?
caseStudies: Anele Mda Tshepo Mogano

title: Dr Uzabakiriho
oneLiner: Its been 30 years since one of the darkest moments in modern history- The Rwandan genocide, but in the midst of these atrocities, as story of hope emerged- The story of Dr Bernard Uzabakiriho.
summary: In 1994, South Africa was filled with hope as we prepared for our first democratic elections. The rallying cry of 'WE ARE FREE AT LAST' symbolized our triumph over oppression. But amidst our celebration, Rwanda faced a devastating genocide, highlighting the failure of global intervention. As we reflect on 30 years since the Rwandan tragedy, we're sadly witnessing history repeating itself. The international community's response falls short once more ( big surprise there !). But amidst all this nonsense happening , there's a story of hope I want to share : Meet Dr. Bernard Uzabakiriho, a gynaecologist oncologist in South Africa. He's one of only thirty-three in the entire country, but his journey to this point began in 1994. Having survived the Rwandan genocide, he found himself in a refugee camp in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There, he witnessed immense suffering, especially among women and children. Despite the odds stacked against him as a 23-year-old refugee surviving on handouts, he dared to dream big. Working in a section of the United Nations High Commission for Refugees, where his job involved clearing dead bodies off the streets due to a cholera outbreak, he persevered. With his earnings, he sought better opportunities, eventually migrating to Zambia and enrolling at Chainama College of Health Sciences. Paying for tuition through his earnings as a hawker and with support from a refugee advocacy organization, he earned a diploma as a Clinical Officer General in 1998. He then secured a job at the University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka. However, he later took a leap of faith and traveled to South Africa in 1999. Arriving in South Africa didn't initially bring the promised opportunities. Dr. Uzabakiriho found himself homeless and working as a car guard just to survive. Despite facing these challenges, he managed to save enough to register at Wits Medical School, although he struggled to pay tuition fees and was nearly deregistered for failing to pay his tuition. Fortunately, a Good Samaritan stepped in, providing surety for his study loan until he completed his Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) degree. He then specialized in obstetrics and gynaecology, eventually qualifying as a gynaecology oncologist in 2022. Today, he serves at Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital in Johannesburg, a testament to his incredible journey of resilience and determination.

title: Child Soldiers
oneLiner: Children carrying guns: The reality of life on the Cape Flats
summary:
The aim of this story is uncover the phenomenon of ‘child soldiers’ on the Cape Flats - whose innocence is lost to the power of a gun, while also asking the important questions of: ‘What do their futures look like?’ ‘Is there any salvation?’ ‘And in a society where gangsterism has become the norm - and the family norm - and violence is entrenched in these communities, is joining a gang their only choice?’ This insert aims to paint a stark but real picture of the role of ‘child soldiers’ in gangs, and take an in-depth look at how schools have now become a paradise for gangsters, a breeding ground for recruits. It will also examine the psychology behind what appeals to children to join these gangs, with a focus on uncovering how they’re recruited; the risks, the prestige, the power they strive for and which most eventually attain; and the sense of belonging they seem to find within these gangs. And it will discuss policing strategies and potential solutions to tackling the scourge, and ensuring that children maintain their innocence.

The Cape Flats are aflame yet again. The gangster protagonists are almost always young men, many still in their teens; warriors in an urban jungle where the police are often scared to enter. This is a story of young boys who spend their pastimes carrying rifles and peddling drugs, instead of playing pretend as superheroes or racing toy cars with friends; where children as young as nine are recruited into gangs and turned into killers. It’s a story of a lost generation of unloved, angry youths, who are growing up with a predisposition towards danger, drugs, and violence.
caseStudies: Craven Engel Jurina de Wee

title: Broken Promises: Eastern Cape
oneLiner: A Trail of Broken Promises and Squandered Funds in the Eastern Cape...
summary:
Amidst the buzz of provincial elections, Carte Blanche sets out to uncover a shadowy reality lurking beneath the surface of the Eastern Cape's development landscape. While the spotlight often shines on big-ticket projects and political promises, our investigation aims to shed light on the trail of incomplete projects left in the wake of mismanagement and controversy. This will be a news report. At the heart of our story are the communities of the Eastern Cape, whose hopes for improved infrastructure and amenities have been dashed by a series of failed projects. From the bustling streets of Centane to the tranquil fields of eNgcobo, we will journey through the province to witness firsthand the remnants of projects that never reached fruition.

Uncovering the hidden realities behind the facade of development in the Eastern Cape and exposing the cost of incomplete projects and hold accountable those responsible for the mismanagement of public funds. The pursuit of accountability for years-old projects that have been abandoned, showcasing the ongoing lack of oversight and transparency in local government spending.
caseStudies: Xolani Somana Tando Tunce Zolile Williams Lungisile Xekethwana

title: Bokkie the Turtle
summary: 21st October 2023, South Africa is on on high after their nail biting win 16 -15 against England. Not 12 hours later barnacle covered turtle is washed up on Struisbaai beach. She’s rescued by a local and contacts Leon Volke, one of the many volunteers up and down South Africa’s coastline. These volunteers make up The Turtle Rescue Network. The Two Oceans Aquarium in Cape Town is where she ends up. Here its also a nail biting couple of days for the aquarium team to see if this barely alive turtle - covered with green algae and barnacles and an amputated front flipper- will survive. Its touch and go but she does and does and is named “Bokkie” in honour of our South African Springboks. This is Bokkies story from her rescue, to her rehabilitation to her soon to be release. Her story will be told by the various people who have been in her life, on land. From the Leon at the rescue; the vet, Bernice; Talitha, who runs the turtle rehab at the aquarium / Aleysha volunteer to the team who release her.
caseStudies: Bokkie Turtle

oneLiner: On the eve of the national election, we take a deep dive into the Northern Cape to look at what exactly the ANC government has done for the people.
summary:
The Northern Cape... a forgotten province

How many broken buildings symbolise the governments' broken promises to its people?

title: Biodiversity Strategy
oneLiner: Biodiversity is big business - a strategy to monetise South Africa's wildlife and plants has divided conservation scientists.
summary:
The Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment ( DFFE ) recently released a 48 page plan on its revised draft National Biodiversity Economy Strategy, which has proved to be extremely controversial among conservationists. The plan was aired at an indaba in Johannesburg in March, where President Cyril Ramaphosa addressed potential investors in the biodiversity economy. He said “lying hidden, like Rembrandts in the attic, are the endowments our people should now utilise – the land, the plants and everything else”. He emphasised the need to empower rural communities, and placed them at the centre of plans to radically transform the biodiversity economy. The plan essentially aims to create mega living conservation landscapes – an increase from 20 million to 34 million hectares by 2040, to attract international trophy hunters, tourists, and investors from abroad. Environmental NGOs are sounding the alarm, and claim that South Africa will become the pariah of the conservation world if this plan is implemented. The plan essentially seeks to create jobs and increase revenue, focussing on rural communities benefitting from the commodification of a wide range of wildlife. This will include an increase in hunting, the slaughter of wild animals as a source of cheaper protein for rural communities, as well as the sale of rhino horn for medicinal purposes to Asian tourists. The domestic trade in ivory will also be stimulated, with ivory being available for purchase by tourists and investors. The plans are ambitious.They include increasing areas under conservation from 20 million hectares to 34 million hectares. And increasing the number of international hunters annually.

South Africa's natural assets ..not just to be admired…but to be more aggressively exploited - for both money and jobs. That’s the Government’s vision for a transformed biodiversity economy - to harness our natural wealth like never before.
caseStudies: Pete Ruinard Hayley Clements

title: Trafficked Part 2
oneLiner: We join police on a pre-dawn raid of a mysterious plot on the outskirts of Pretoria - the suspected hideout of a criminal gang dealing in forged passports, stolen cars and illegal scrap metal
summary:
This could possibly stand as a stand alone story or part of a bigger follow up story to our Trafficked piece.

We have been given an exclusive opportunity to join the SAPS National Joint Operations Command on the pre dawn raid. The sight is the suspected manufacturing facility for forged travel documents like SA Id's and passports. Also home to suspected criminals such as carjackers and illegal copper dealers. Also on site, about 70 undocumented foreign nationals from countries like Malawi and Zimbabwe. The SAPS team is apparently going to be quite a force - more than a hundred members including Tactical Response and the National Intervention Unit. Depending on what happens at the property and what is found, the SAPS are planning on making further arrests at multiple locations.

title: Operation Racketeer
oneLiner: Rogue cops, an antipoaching unit, extrajudicial killings to claim bonuses and danger pay. The story of two building contractors and a good cop, whose lives were destroyed when they were set up as rhin
summary:
Overview Around 2014, police officer Christopher Gumbi was seconded to take part in a rural safety operation in the Jozini cluster. He had already been involved in the process of gathering information about an operation involving the rendition of foreign nationals from Mozambique being lured into game parks in KZN and then killing them under the guise of those persons being suspected of being involved in rhino horn poaching. The purpose of the persons involved in the rendition and the murder of foreign nationals was to recover rewards paid to informers and recover danger allowances. But Gumbi was a problem to a group of police and private security who had a lot to hide and a lot to lose, because they were doing just that- cashing in on money from an NGO and danger pay from the police, by falsely accusing innocent victims of rhino poaching. Their victims -and the stories of Wiseman Mageba and Dumisani Gwala if exposed would pose a threat to the rogue police and their security buddies who claim to be hero’s saving the rhino, when all they were really doing was lining their own pockets. Our story weaves Gumbi’s story with that of Gwala and Mageba. All three have been vindicated by the courts and we have all the documents. Gumbi has already been paid damages, but he left the police. In July 2023 Gwala and Mageba were vindicated by the courts and now they have in Feb 2024 served summons against SAPS and the NPA for a large damages claim.

The case studies will go on camera, we have unseen footage, and all the court documents vindicating the men who claimed innocence for over 9 years but were smeared by an NGO with ulterior motives.
caseStudies: Dumisani Gwala Wiseman Mageba Christopher Gumbi
experts: Megan Carr - may use a pseudonym

title: THROW-FORWARD: The decay of public spaces
oneLiner: Johannesburg's public spaces are visibly decaying, becoming the territory of transient people with nowhere else to go. How can the City and its formal residents balance compassion for the homeless wit
summary:
A failing economy is driving more and more people into poverty, accelerating the influx of desperate people into middle-class suburbs and their civic spaces. Streets, parks and public buildings are increasingly being appropriated by waste pickers, transient people and opportunistic criminals. Authorities' failure to enforce by-laws hastens the degradation of these important public spaces, and the risk to residents and small businesses is ever increasing.

Carte Blanche grapples with the impact of homelessness on public spaces, a complex problem with no obvious and easy solutions.

title: Anti microbial resistance: Threat to humanity.
oneLiner: Will so called super bugs become the biggest threat to humanity in the twenty first century?
summary:
Superbugs are strains of bacteria, viruses, parasites and fungi that are resistant to most of the antibiotics and other medications commonly used to treat the infections they cause. A few examples of superbugs include resistant bacteria that can cause pneumonia, urinary tract infections and skin infections. Research has show that to date, the environment has been the neglected component in the one-health triad, One health triad being human, animal and environment. The transmission of AMR is probably multi-directional, Research is currently being done on wastewater as well as soil that’s been fertilised with the manure from pigs and poultry fed with antimicrobials as well as environmental surveillance within wastewater close to informal settlements and hospital effluent and wastewater treatment plants, focusing on the environmental dimensions.

The threat of so-called super bugs is a major challenge facing humanity in the twenty-first century. That is according to the World Health Organisation. The misuse and overuse of antibiotics in medicine and food production has created antimicrobial resistance making some diseases almost untreatable leading to millions of deaths in the future.
caseStudies: Ingrid Schoeman Vanessa Carter

title: Sifiso Mkhwanazi
summary: Joburg prowler Sifiso Mkhwanazi In the heart of downtown Joburg, a series of gruesome murders sends shockwaves through the community. The perpetrator, known as Sifiso Mkhwanazi, emerges as a shadowy figure, leaving behind a trail of death and devastation. As law enforcement agencies scramble to apprehend the elusive killer, a chilling portrait begins to emerge of a man driven by dark impulses and a twisted sense of purpose…Found guilty of killing 6 sex workers , and the possibility of many more victims, we look into what drove one of the country’s youngest serial killers and the investigation that led to his arrest.
caseStudies: Nokuthula Khumalo Grace Moyo

title: Mhlengi Gwala
summary:
Mhlengi Gwala After nearly losing his life, exactly 5 years ago, triathlete Mhlengi Gwala had to use every ounce of his strength to fight for his life first, to survive and to compete again. His story made international headlines in 2018 after criminals attacked him with a chainsaw that cut off 80% of his leg leaving him for dead. Two years later, in 2020, his leg caught infection and had to be amputated. Throughout all this, Mhlengi could only think of one way out…to go back to his old life of alcohol and drugs and totally forget about this dream - to be one of the top triathletes in the world. It was three people who kept him away from a life of self-destruction; his mother, children, and friends - they kept reminding him of his greatness and that he could do it again. Sport, he says, is the only thing he knows, and without it life would have no meaning. It’s been a turbulent five years of stops and starts and in October 2023, he fnally picked his shoes to compete fully without any disruptions and to focus on his dreams; to compete in the 2024 Paralympics games. Mhlengi believes he will and is currently in the UAE and Australia for his Paralympic qualification. Mhlengi hopes to forgive and forget the past five years which he considers the most horrible time of his life. On top of dealing with the trauma of his attack and losing his leg, he still faced more challenges like nearly losing his other good leg after an accident at work as a lifeguard and an almost a-year ban for a banned substance. Mhlengi still wonders if he will ever get justice as the criminals have never been caught.

After suffering numerous misfortunes including his amputated leg, Mhlengi Gwala fights to compete again.
caseStudies: Mhlengi Gwala Bafundi Magwaza

title: Tammy Taylor 4
oneLiner: Peet Viljoen the disbarred lawyer has been spreading fake news to minor online publications. We correct the lies and give you the facts.
summary:
A three minute tongue-in-cheek take-down of mini-celebrity and 7th housewife Peet Viljoen, addressing lie for lie his desperate attempt to remain relevant. NO presenter, only for voice over. We also play the video which recorded the conversation between myself and the police officers and proves that there was no defamation.

We name and shame the online publications: Dubai Daily, Netwerk24, Beeld, Find-It.

title: Trading sham: A market for counterfeit goods
oneLiner: The underground world of trading in counterfeit products cost the economy billions but what may be unbeknown to many, is that buying cheap may cost you your life.
summary:
There is a counterfeit product for nearly every real product in South Africa. And although the laws here are strict and curbs the illegal trade to an extend, criminality still manages to seep through the gaps, and this cost the South African economy billions of Rands.

Fake brands of well known house products come at a cheap price on the black market. But these days, even well-known and trusted medicine brands are hitting the shelves... replicated and manufactured in backyard factories. Saving a few bucks can be a fatal decision.
